items.statement: Full-year volume growth over FY26 maintained
items.quote: Yes, we are maintaining the full year volume, and we'll be having a growth over last year by the year-end.

items.statement: Capex target INR15,000 cr for FY27, rising to INR20,000+ cr in FY28 and INR25,000-26,000 cr thereafter
items.quote: So far as capex is concerned, this year, we're planning a target of INR15,000 crores, and this is going to increase in the next 2, 3 years because our expanses are on. That means next year, it could be in excess of INR20,000 crores. And after that maybe INR25,000 crores, INR26,000 crores like that.

items.statement: Durgapur TMT bar mill (0.8-0.9 mtpa) expected Sep-Dec 2027 to convert excess semis
items.quote: And that is expected sometime in 2027, maybe September to December 2027, that is the expectation.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA INR4,356 cr, up >50% YoY; margin 16.7%, best since FY22; EBITDA/t INR10,464
items.quote: EBITDA at INR4,356 crores showed for quarter 1 '26-'27 has a growth of more than 50% as compared to CPLY figure of INR2,925 crores. EBITDA margin at 16.7% is one of the best since '21-'22, when the steel market at that time was at its peak and coal price was at its bottom in '21-'22. EBITDA per tonne also crossed a benchmark figure of INR10,000 per tonne and stood at INR10,464 per tonne in quarter

items.statement: Q1 avg NSR INR57,100/t vs Q4 INR52,000/t (+INR5,100); July NSR INR55,600 (flat INR56,900, long INR54,200)
items.quote: Quarter 1 average NSR was INR57,100 as compared to quarter 4 of INR52,000 that means an increase of around INR5,000 per tonne between these 2.

items.statement: Q2 NSR expected down INR1,000-2,000/t vs Q1; long products may recover INR500-1,000 from July lows
items.quote: So kind of -- if you talk about quarter 2, quarter 2 NSR as compared to quarter 1 could be down by around INR1,000 to INR2,000, maybe. This is just a guesswork.

items.statement: Imported coking coal cost Q1 INR21,300/t vs Q4 INR18,100/t; index fell from 235 to 220; Q2 consumption cost seen down INR1,000-1,500/t
items.quote: Yes, yes, it will reduce because now the price is softening, so it will reduce only. Maybe there will be a reduction of around INR1,000 to INR1,500 in Q2 compared to Q1.

items.statement: Indigenous coal 15% of blend (5% captive at INR13,100/t vs imported INR21,200/t); captive share to rise from Dec as Tasra ramps (cost ~INR5,000-6,000/t)
items.quote: So out of that 15%, we get somewhere around 5% from our own mines and which is likely to go up from December onwards becau se production from Tasra mines, which is under development right now is going to take place in the month of -- expectedly in the month of December

items.statement: Q1 sales mix: flat 52.7%, long 34.8%, semis 12.5% (down from 14%); finished steel share up to 89% from 86%
items.quote: It's almost kind of 50% -50%. And one thing is that the semis have come down. The semis have come down from, say, 14% last quarter 1 to 11% this quarter 1 and between long and flat, t he long is -- flat is 52.7%, long is 34.8% and semis are at 12.5% in quarter 1

items.statement: Iron ore sales Q1: 1.1 mt (vs 0.31 mt YoY), revenue INR574 cr (vs INR157 cr), EBITDA ~INR150 cr; FY27 target 8 mt
items.quote: So volumes are 1.1 million tonnes. And last year, quarter 1 was 0.31 million tonnes. And when it is 1.1 million tonnes this quarter, last year, we sold around 3 -odd million tonnes, although we are targeting a very high target of 8 million tonnes, let's see how far we can go.

items.statement: Sub-grade fines inventory 32 mt; 3 mt auctioned in Q1 (target for FY27); Chhattisgarh auctions fructified, Jharkhand efforts ongoing
items.quote: We are having a volume of around 32 million tonnes inventory in the balance sheet. And we have put up in the auction around 3 million tonnes. The rates are yet to come, and we are hopeful that this time, we'll be able to click that particular thing. So th at will become a beginning of selling -- of our efforts towards selling 32 million tonnes going forward

items.statement: Inventory up 0.2 mt in Q1; borrowings flat at INR21,729 cr (vs INR21,663 cr 1-Mar); aim to reduce inventory in H2 and cut working capital borrowings
items.quote: And when we look at the borrowing po sition as on 30th June 2026 at the end of this quarter, we are almost at the same level as that of the beginning of this year in spite of the fact that the inventory has increased by 0.2 million

items.statement: Debt/equity 0.36 (down from ~0.38-0.39); cost of debt 6.24% (vs 6.8% YoY), saving INR100 cr in Q1 finance cost; debt further down to INR21,400 cr currently
items.quote: The debt equity ratio has come down to 0.36, maybe from 0.38 or 0.39 in the opening of this year. So deleveraging efforts are on. And so far as today's position is conc erned, the debt has further come down to a level of INR21,400 crores

items.statement: Safeguard duty 11.5% continues (year 2 of 3); anti-dumping investigation underway, may provide relief
items.quote: In safeguard front, actually, yes, there is a step. Safeguard is still in place, which is 11.5% as of now because it was there for 3 years, and now we are in the second year right now. So that still continued. It is giving a relief to the -- much needed relief to the stee l domestic market. So far as antidumping thing is concerned, that is going on. And based on the investigation, maybe some measu

items.statement: Rail provisional price for FY27 currently INR74,000/t; final price expected in FY28, seen higher due to higher coal costs
items.quote: So for the year '26-'27 because the imported coal prices are on the higher side and our provisional price is pretty low at INR74,000. So we are expecting a better price compared to that. And so that is going to improve our profitability whenever it is declared.

items.statement: Employee cost Q1 INR2,937 cr (flat YoY); VRS ongoing, headcount falling; wage revision provision to be evaluated in Q4
items.quote: Salary basis this year in quarter 1 i s INR2,937 crores as compared to last year's figure of INR2,944 crores, almost at the same level. While in this quarter 1, it includes the VR -- differential VR amount, VRS Voluntary Retirement because our VRS scheme is on. So many people have taken VRS. That factor is also there in the employee remuneration. The number of employees are coming down and VRS is

items.statement: Primary-secondary TMT price gap narrowed to ~INR5,000/t, supporting primary NSR uptick
items.quote: So now the gap has narrowed down. The gap is around INR5,000 right now, which is a healthy gap. So that's the reason why probably there is an uptick in the NSR in the prices of the primary TMT products.

items.statement: Logistics constraints persist for iron ore evacuation; mitigating via more rakes and road transport
items.quote: Logistics constraint is still there. We are trying to buy with that through better availability of rakes as well as by increasing, enhancing our quantities through road. So those are the efforts we are making so that the logistics constraints to some extent can be eased out.

items.statement: Indian steel consumption grew >8% YoY in Q1 FY27; production up ~3%; net imports 0.4-0.5 mt vs 0.3 mt YoY
items.quote: Indian steel industry, however, continues to enjoy robust demand for steel with consumption during quarter 1 '26 -'27, which has grown by more than 8% over CPLY. The production, however, showed a muted slightly l ower growth of around 3% during this year -- during this quarter '26-'27

items.statement: Cost reduction target INR2,000-3,000/t in FY27; by FY29 net saving ~INR2,000/t after IISCO expansion (variable -INR4,000, fixed +INR1,500-2,000)
items.quote: See, we are looking at a cost reduction of around INR2,000 to INR3,000 in this year itself. In quarter 1, because most of our -- many of our uni ts are down because of the advancement of the capital, the cost was a little on the higher side. So from quarter 2 onwards because all the mills and facilities are in place so far . So cost reduction efforts will be there and the cost reduction will be th

items.statement: Q1 crude steel 4.8 mt (-0.1 mt YoY), sales 4.2 mt (-7-8% YoY); capital repairs advanced at IISCO, Durgapur, Bokaro by design
items.quote: Crude steel production stood at 4.8 million tonnes in quarter 1 '26 -'27 as against 4.9 million tonnes CPLY. This reduction is because of the capital repairs which have been advanced in this quar ter 1 by design. Sales volume was 4.2 million tonnes, which fell by around 7% to 8% as compared to the previous

items.statement: Export Stationery revenue guided at 5% degrowth for FY27
items.quote: This year, as I just mentioned, overall, we are seeing degrowth of around 5% compared to last year.

items.statement: Domestic Stationery revenue growth guided at 15% to 17% for FY27
items.quote: In Domestic Stationery, we are looking growth of around 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Stationery segment EBITDA margin guided at around 12% for FY27
items.quote: On the Stationery front, I am expecting around 12% margin.

items.statement: Publication division EBITDA margin guided at 26%-27% for FY27
items.quote: Publication, the margins would be around 26%-27%.

items.statement: Combined Stationery EBITDA margin guided at 10%-11% sustainable level
items.quote: If we talk about both Stationery businesses together, we should do between 10% and 11% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Curriculum changes in Maharashtra and Gujarat caused spillover of Publication revenue from Q1 to Q2 FY27
items.quote: Because of this timing difference, our real growth is not fully reflected in the 1st Quarter numbers.

items.statement: Domestic Stationery grew 26% in Q1 FY27 driven by paper stationery, brand association, cover designs, e-commerce and quick commerce
items.quote: The standout star of the quarter was Domestic Stationery experiencing 26% surge.

items.statement: Export Stationery contracted around 9% in Q1 FY27 due to supply chain disruptions, geopolitical challenges and weakening US demand
items.quote: Export Stationery contracted by around 9%.

items.statement: Stationery segment margin compressed in Q1 FY27 due to discounted export pricing from tariffs and under-absorbed overheads from polymer plant underutilization
items.quote: Once tariffs were withdrawn, and it takes a couple of weeks to get settled. And then we started realizing the normal pricing. And therefore, that was one of the reasons of lower margin in Stationery.

items.statement: Publication Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin around 40% but seasonal; Q2 margin expected higher year-on-year but lower sequentially due to fixed cost absorption
items.quote: Publication business, it was around 40%, but it again, it gets majority of the business.

items.statement: Polymer plant investment of Rs. 65 crores started in Q4 FY26; capacity utilization only around 30% in Q1 FY27 due to weak export orders and high polymer prices
items.quote: total investment in the plant is around Rs. 65 crores and with the teams there. So, total utilization wise, this plant just started in last quarter of FY26

items.statement: Polymer plant capacity utilization around 30% in Q1 FY27; under-absorbed overheads compressed Stationery segment profitability
items.quote: Capacity wise, we would have hardly used around 30%-odd capacity of that plant. And because of that, all manpower cost, as well as overall factory overheads, that took away the margin in the current business.

items.statement: Publication Q2 FY27 revenue expected to reach Rs. 130+ crores vs Rs. 91 crores in Q2 FY26 due to curriculum change spillover
items.quote: So, Rs. 91 crores will definitely go above Rs. 130 odd crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 total revenue expected around Rs. 300+ crores vs Rs. 247 crores in Q2 FY26 due to Publication spillover
items.quote: Overall Rs. 247 crores should reach Rs. 300 odd crore.

items.statement: Paper prices increased around Rs. 2000 per ton (~2%) since April 2026; further hikes announced but not implemented due to market conditions
items.quote: Yes, there was around Rs. 2000 per ton around that much increment was there since April.

items.statement: Non-paper stationery currently small but targeted to reach 10%-15% of Domestic Stationery in 3 years; new categories launching by end of FY27
items.quote: In 3 years' time, it will be of that percentage we are very confident of. Recently what we just did was whatever product that we already had in non-paper which was not paid attention by us that we changed overall look, feel, packaging, everything of that, introduced several other product range in the same category. But the new categories will be made available at the end of this year.

items.statement: US retailers holding high channel inventory due to inflationary pressure; reorder quantities not encouraging
items.quote: Channel inventory, majorly the inventory with our purchasers because there is no one in the channel. It is us and directly the major retailers of the US. So, they are still left out with the inventory. It is the upliftment is not like as usual, as I just said, because of the inflationary pressure. And therefore, the reorder numbers, quantities are not encouraging as it used to be earlier.

items.statement: State board schools transitioning to CBSE curriculum growing >15% YoY; Navneet and Indiannica now have full portfolio for CBSE schools up to grade 10
items.quote: Generally trend wise, I am saying that the growth in such schools is more than 15% year-on-year. So, that way more and more English mediums schools which are state affiliated are transitioning to CBSE type of curriculum.

items.statement: No clarity yet from Gujarat government on curriculum changes for next financial year
items.quote: It means there is no clarity from the state government itself till now for the next year.

items.statement: US remains dominant export market (~75% of stationery exports); other markets growing but still negligible share
items.quote: Even though we have grown in other markets a little bit, but compared to US, as a percentage, that remains negligible.

items.statement: Sold 4.5% stake in K-12 for Rs. 330 crores post-Q1; remaining stake 8.8%; proceeds kept for potential inorganic opportunities in domestic stationery
items.quote: 4.5% we are selling and how much will we be left with? Kalpesh Dedhia: It will be around 8.8% we will be having with us

items.statement: No plans for financial investments; Rs. 330 crore proceeds from K-12 stake sale retained for quick inorganic decisions in domestic stationery
items.quote: We don't want to become financial investors in any company now. As far as the utilization of these funds are concerned, of course, we are very clear that going forward, we want to grow Indian market to its full potential in Stationery segment. And therefore, apart from organic, there could be some inorganic opportunities also may come nothing on the table right now but we want to have this balance

items.statement: Aggressive investments in branding and appointment of additional senior talent for Non-Paper Stationery vertical
items.quote: To sustain this momentum, we have initiated a long-term strategic plan. And this includes aggressive investments in branding and the key appointment of additional senior talent specifically for our Non-Paper Stationery vertical.

items.statement: Workbooks constitute ~45% of Publication revenue, majorly driven by school recommendations
items.quote: Overall, I can tell you that of the total Publication revenue, around 45% comes from the workbook category. And you can say major of that is due to recommendation by the respective schools.

items.statement: Export Stationery back-to-school season business lost permanently due to tariff disruptions and US inflation; cannot be spilled over to later quarters
items.quote: And there are major our back-to-school season, which already went by, wherein because of these challenges, we could not supply as usual. And that business cannot just get spilled over. And therefore, that we have lost that business.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions in Gulf region post-May 2026 caused renewed uncertainty and order cancellations from US customers
items.quote: Post my May call, again there were various disruptions and uncertainty again emerged in the Gulf. And because of that, the main affected country, I would say, apart from Iran, is US. And therefore, so many dynamics have changed in this period with newer and newer decisions coming in regularly.

items.statement: Poultry Healthcare Division grew 48% YoY driven by higher institutional business, deeper market penetration, and stronger customer engagement
items.quote: The Poultry Healthcare Division delivered an excellent quarter, recording 48% growth over the corresponding quarter of the previous y ear. The growth was supported by higher institutional business, deeper market penetration and continued strengthening of customer engagement across key markets

items.statement: Standalone gross margins improved from 69% to 78% due to favorable product mix and operational efficiencies
items.quote: Gross margins improved from 69% to 78%, which was mainly supported by a favorable product mix and our continued efforts on operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Animal Healthcare Division impacted by timing delays in government immunization programs (PPR eradication and Lumpy Skin Disease Control Initiative)
items.quote: The Animal Healthcare Division continued to be impacted by the timing of government-led immunization programs, particularly under the PPR eradication and the Lumpy Skin Disease Control Initiative, for which we supply our Goat Pox vaccine.

items.statement: Early traction in Poultry Health Products Portfolio (feed supplements, disinfectants) complementing vaccine business with holistic disease prevention approach
items.quote: We are also encouraged by the early traction witnessed in the Poultry Health Products Portfolio introduced during the previous financial year, including feed supplements and disinfectant solutions.

items.statement: BSL3 and fill-finish facilities included in ~65% overall capacity utilization; manufacturing setup fungible between poultry and large animal vaccines
items.quote: Yes, it comprises of the entire manufacturing setup, the number that we gave, which is an approximate number, but yes, keeping into mind the entire manufacturing setup.

items.statement: Overall plant capacity utilization at 60-65% across poultry, large animal, and pet vaccine production with varying dose sizes
items.quote: Our capacity utilization over here at the plant, it is at around 60% to 65%. Now, these terms, again, are very subjective. Poultry vaccines are being produced, large animals are being produced, 1000 doses are being produced, 25 doses are being produced, pet vaccines are being produced, single dose, 5 doses, 1000, 2000 doses of poultry.

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced to Rs. 103 crores as of June 30, 2026 after Hester Africa loan restructuring with Gates Foundation
items.quote: The consolidated debt as on 30th June is Rs. 103 crores.

items.statement: Low pathogenic avian influenza vaccine approved in March 2026 showing good market response and contributing to poultry division growth
items.quote: The market response has been very good, I would say. And we are selling this vaccine. And I think, I mean, to answer your question, in one sentence, the market response is very good.

items.statement: Africa operations face geopolitical and economic volatility; demand exists but ability to pay constrained; no directional guidance provided
items.quote: Today, the world is volatile, forget about other markets. This is too precise for us to answer. We will take it as it comes. And there is a demand, we will meet the demand. Sometimes demand is ability as well as willingness. Willingness is there, ability may not be there, etc., etc., because of these geopolitical reasons.

items.statement: Receivables slightly higher due to seasonal issues but manageable; positive operating cash flow maintained
items.quote: Receivables are a little higher. Sometimes this is due to seasonal issues and all. It's a trend which goes on, but we don't see this as a concern at all. And it's not even a red flag or anythin g of a concern to us. It's going on perfectly

items.statement: Brucella recombinant vaccine development progressing on timeline; updates to be shared at appropriate regulatory stages
items.quote: Brucella recombinant vaccine development is going in proper timeline. There is significant progress as a nd when we have appropriate information to give up in the public domain, we will give it

items.statement: Poultry vaccines sold through same distribution network as health products; no separate network for cross-selling feed supplements and disinfectants
items.quote: No, there is no different network. It is the same network, which sells vaccines and health products. So, it is one distribution network all across.

items.statement: Poultry vaccines manufactured across India, Nepal, and Africa facilities; poultry market significant in all three countries
items.quote: In Africa and Nepal, yes, we are supplying the poultry vaccines and we manufacture in Africa plus India and N epal, poultry vaccines are manufactured across all three facilities and the poultry market is huge in all these

items.statement: Pet care division emerging with antibiotics, anti-parasitics, grooming products; not reported separately until meaningful scale achieved
items.quote: Pet division is our new division. It's right now emerging. Of course, as we all know, pet care in general, pet h ealthcare, has many segments to it. There is quite a bit of competition also. At this point in time, we do not report it separately. It is a part of our animal health business

items.statement: Targets INR5,000 crores revenue by FY29 over next three years
items.quote: we see our company as a INR5,000 crores company in the next three years.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve gradually quarter-on-quarter as raw material prices ease and KUSUM 2.0 launches
items.quote: Going forward, with KUSUM 2.0 expected to come in and raw material prices likely to ease as the geopolitical situation stabilizes, we expect margins to improve gradually on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Total capex of INR1,500-1,700 crores by September 2027, split roughly 50-50 between this year and next
items.quote: By September 2027, we have to complete all these capex. So, almost the capex of INR1,500 to INR1,700 crores is to be completed in this time period.

items.statement: 0.5 GW DCR module facility completion by September 2026, 2.2 GW integrated cell and module by September 2027
items.quote: We have two facilities coming up. One is fo r 0.5 GW which will be completed in September '26. The second is for 2.2 GW, for which we are aiming at September '27

items.statement: Order book of approximately INR1,000 crores as of 22nd July 2026, executable in next two quarters
items.quote: We continue to maintain a healthy and diversified order book of approximately INR1,000 crores as on 22nd July 2026.

items.statement: Export order inflows around INR100 crores per quarter
items.quote: So, every quarter we are getting orders of around INR100 crores for the export business.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 9.6% sequentially stable; YoY pressure from 6% raw material cost increase and 4% lower realization
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin remained broadly stable on a sequential basis at 9.6%.

items.statement: Raw material impact INR36 crores (6%), lower realization impact INR25 crores (4%) on EBITDA YoY
items.quote: In absolute terms, this translated into an EBITDA impact of around INR36 crores from raw material costs and INR25 crores from sales price realization.

items.statement: Targets 15% EBITDA margin for rooftop business post module integration
items.quote: And in this, if we combine the current industry benchmark and module, we are targeting around 15%.

items.statement: Solar pump volumes up 57.6% YoY to 27,678 pumps in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we achieved strong momentum in solar pump installations, with volume increasing by 57.6% year-on-year to 27,678 pumps in Q1 FY27 compared to 17,557 pumps in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: PM KUSUM 2.0 ready for launch, could be announced as early as next week or next month, currently with PMO
items.quote: PM KUSUM 2.0 is ready for launch and could be announced as early as next week or next month. It is currently with the PMO and awaiting clearance from there.

items.statement: Feeder-level solarization expected to drive additional pump demand
items.quote: Feeder-level solarization is ex pected to drive additional demand for pumps, thereby creating a larger opportunity for us

items.statement: Rooftop revenue INR8 crores in Q1 FY27 vs INR2 crores YoY; cash and retail sales INR24 crores
items.quote: The rooftop business in this quarter showed a healthy growth. We clocked INR8 crores revenue as compared to INR2 crores in a like-to-like quarter last year.

items.statement: EV motors in validation and testing phase for next 8-9 months, meaningful revenue from FY28
items.quote: The product is currently in the validation and testing phase, which is a time-taking process. We expect this phase to continue for the next eight to nine months. Revenue should begin to ramp up gradually thereafter, with meaningful contribution expected from next year onwards.

items.statement: Realization per pump flat QoQ at INR248,153 vs INR248,374; minor mix impact from KUSUM and Magel Tyala orders
items.quote: This quarter, the realization is at INR248,153 and last quarter it was INR248,374. So, there is no big impact. The minor impact is due to the sales mix.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased 6% YoY (stainless steel, copper, aluminium, mild steel); recently softened by INR1-1.5
items.quote: The 6% raw material impact we faced was largely due to increases in stainless steel, copper, aluminium, and mild steel prices amid the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Working capital limits of ~INR1,800 crores from 10 Indian banks and one Qatar bank; term loan of ~INR800 crores for 2.2 GW project
items.quote: First, on working capital, we have arrangements with around 10 leading banks in India and one bank from Qatar, providing us with sufficient working capital limits of approximately INR1,800 crores. In addition, for the 2.2 GW solar project, we have also entered into a term loan arrangement of around INR800 crores

items.statement: Promoter holding stable, increased after QIPs; no hedging on raw materials as viewed temporary
items.quote: No, we are not taking any he dging position right now because we are looking at it as a temporary situation

items.statement: Export business steady despite geopolitical uncertainties; war in Middle East not impacting business
items.quote: No, that's why we have maintained our growth in exports as well. The war has not had that much of an impact; it hasn't affected our business.

items.statement: Registered as brand owner in PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana; inverter feedback shows 10% better generation
items.quote: We've taken the initiative to be a brand owner in the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. We have registered ourselves.

items.statement: Does not comment on peers' margins; focuses on service quality, product quality, brand strength in rate contract model
items.quote: We can only talk about our margins. We have been an industry experience for 40 years. We don't comment on peers.

items.statement: Government focus on quality, digitalization, end-to-end warranty in PM Surya Ghar next phase benefits Shakti
items.quote: In the next phase, in consultations with various stakeholders, it's clear that the focus areas are quality, digitaliza tion, and customer experience by providing end-to-end warranty

items.statement: PAT INR52 crores in Q1 FY27, up 35% QoQ; PAT margin 6% vs 4.5% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: During Q1 FY27, the company reported a PAT of INR52 crores, representing an increase of 35% over Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Views margin pressure as temporary and external, driven by geopolitical situation; no structural issue
items.quote: we view these margin pressures as temporary and largely external in nature, rather than reflective of any structural issue in the business.

items.statement: Two QIPs completed (INR200 crores first QIP); internal equity maintained for solar project with bank arrangements
items.quote: For the whole expansion, as we have told you, we have done two QIPs. One was for INR200 crores in which we didn't take any loan, so sufficient funds are available there.

items.statement: Advances growth target 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27
items.quote: With respect to advances, we should be 2 %-3% over and above the credit growth of the industry.

items.statement: NIM expected in 3.65-3.70% range for next few quarters
items.quote: Hence, we expect largely the NIM to be in the range of 3.65% to 3.70% in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected at 47-48% for FY27
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio will remain in the range of 47% to 48% for FY27.

items.statement: Slippages expected at Rs 700-750 crores for FY27 (1.20-1.30% of advances)
items.quote: I think we are on Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 750 crores of the number which we discussed. I think the slippages would be in the same range.

items.statement: ECLGS portfolio expected at Rs 2,000-2,500 crores total
items.quote: So, we expect ECLGS to be in the range of Rs. 2,000 crores to Rs. 2,500 crores totally for this under the scheme.

items.statement: MSME growth expected 2-3% above system credit growth
items.quote: We envisage this to grow 2%, 3% more than the system growth. That's our expectation on this.

items.statement: Gold loan share expected at 31-32% of book
items.quote: We are at 30 %, 31% as we speak today, and we expect it to be in the same range of 31%, 32%.

items.statement: NIM at 3.78% in 1QFY27, expected to moderate by 5 bps
items.quote: Our NIM for 1QFY27 stood at 3.78%. With term deposit rates on the verge of rising due to high demand, we expect the cost of deposits may slightly increase in the next few quarters, which will impact NIM levels by around 5 bps.

items.statement: Advances grew 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crores in 1QFY27
items.quote: For 1QFY27 as well, we have achieved 25% credit growth quarter-on-quarter, the highest growth rate in June-to-June and our advances had increased to Rs. 67,645 crores from Rs. 54,020 crores in 1QFY26.

items.statement: Deposits grew 21% YoY to Rs 79,342 crores in 1QFY27
items.quote: Our deposits stood at Rs. 79,342 crores for 1QFY27 as compared to Rs. 65,734 crores in 1QFY26, registering a growth of 21%.

items.statement: Average CASA grew 22% YoY to Rs 20,062 crores in 1QFY27
items.quote: The average CASA grew by 22% in 1QFY27 to Rs. 20,062 crores compared to Rs. 16,478 in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Gross NPA reduced to 1.73% in 1QFY27 from 2.99% in 1QFY26
items.quote: Our Gross NPA has reduced to 1.73% in 1QFY27. Both Gross NPA and Net NPA, in both percentage and absolute terms, have been reducing quarter-by-quarter for the past 12 quarters continuously.

items.statement: Slippages Rs 195 crores, recoveries Rs 206 crores in 1QFY27
items.value: Rs. 195 crores slippages, Rs. 206 crores recoveries
items.quote: For the current quarter, the total slippages are around Rs. 195 crores, while the total recovery is Rs. 206 crores, consisting of Rs. 182 crores of live NPA and Rs. 24 crores of technically written-off accounts.

items.statement: PCR with technical write-offs at 85% in 1QFY27 vs 79% YoY

items.quote: I think I'm really confident with the kind of product lineup we have ready for Q3. That gives me a lot of confidence. items.quote: So, we will continue to invest in branding campaigns in the upcoming quarter as well in the form of building more consideration and conversion -led campaigns and not a top -of-the-mind campaign, which we have already done. So, let's say, it would be somewhere close to INR7,000 for a Tier 3, INR8,500 for a Tier 2 and maybe INR10,000 - INR10,500 for a Tier 1. So that is first. The other thing is that in our case, franchisees have made a great ROI over t

items.statement: GST impact on gross margin: Q1 FY27 not yet in GST base (implemented end-Sep 2025); full impact from Q3 FY27; Q1 gross margin 65.7% vs 65% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: And just adding to the point, I think GST was implemented sometime in Q3. So, I think it was end September. So Q1 of this year is not part of the GST base yet. I think starting Q3, it's all in the base.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: revenue over INR4,700 crores (42% YoY), EBITDA over INR200 crores (65% YoY), PAT over INR100 crores (50% YoY), exit EBITDA margin over 5%, ROE expanding to almost 13%
items.value: Revenue >4700 cr, EBITDA >200 cr, PAT >100 cr
items.quote: For FY27, excluding our investment businesses: we intend to cross of over INR4,700 crores of revenue, growing 42% year-on-year, EBITDA of over INR200 crores, growing by 65% year-on-year, and PAT of over INR100 crores, growing by 50% year-on-year.

items.statement: Completed STEAG acquisition on May 21, 2026; STEAG consolidated from that date; LSG Sky Chefs India acquisition expected to close in next couple of weeks for INR166 crores including cash
items.quote: We've concluded the acquisition of STEAG Energy Services India Private Limited, or STEAG, on May 21, 2026 , and the numbers o f STEAG have been consolidated from that date in our financials

items.statement: STEAG won 4 large multi-year deals contributing over INR5,100 crores to top line over next 5 years; 3 deals live from July 1, 4th from first week of August
items.quote: As announced earlier, we won 4 large multi-year deals at STEAG, which would contribute to over INR 5,100 crores to Bluspring's top line over the next 5 years.

items.statement: STEAG order book over INR5,200 crores; expected to contribute ~INR1,000 crores revenue in FY27 at 7-8% EBITDA margin
items.quote: For the current year, STEAG with this order book and some of these large mobilizations have already begun from 1st of July and some of it beginning from 1st of August, the overall number from STEAG from a revenue standpoint should be close to around INR1,000 crores in the current year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 3.8% vs 3.1% YoY; Facility & Food 4.6% (flat YoY), Security 2.8%, Smart Infra 9.3% vs 8.2% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 3.8% as compared to 3.1% during the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Security services target 4-4.5% EBITDA margin in next couple of years (from ~3% currently); Facility Management target ~5% (from ~4.6%); Food mix shift to aviation catering for higher margins
items.quote: Our North Star for security industry is to go from the present margins to 4%, 4.5% margins in next couple of years.

items.statement: Telecom capex revival signs from July; expect better H2 FY27 for telecom vertical; Industrial growth driven by manufacturing push in India and Middle East normalization
items.quote: We see some early signs in the month of July of new rollouts coming in for almost all large players. So, we are hopeful that the second half of the year including quarter 2 for telecom should be better.

items.statement: No major capex guidance given; focus on integrating acquisitions, repaying acquisition debt aggressively, and unlocking synergies
items.quote: We will also focus on integrating the two acquired entities, aggressively repaying the acquisition debt, and unlock synergies with our existing core businesses in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Gross debt ~INR307 crores, cash ~INR135 crores, net debt ~INR172 crores; target FY27 exit net debt/EBITDA below 1; acquisition debt ~INR150 crores by year-end, organic debt zero at closing but average INR150-175 crores
items.quote: We are confident of ending the financial year with net debt to EBITDA ratio below 1.

items.statement: Organic working capital days at 37 days; consolidated expected to rise to ~45 days due to STEAG and large industrial contracts; no large funded deposits, only bank guarantees
items.quote: We foresee that it should be closed around 45 days and the water should settle down there, including the large contracts that we have won.

items.statement: Client retention 95% (lose 4-5% annually); new client revenue contribution ~10% YoY; existing client mining adds 8-10% YoY; organic revenue growth guided at 15-16% ex-acquisitions
items.quote: Our retention, which is one of the key KPIs which we monitor internally when it comes to, let's say, losing clients year-on-year, our retention is at a very hea lthy percentage of 95%, and new revenues every year contribute almost 10

items.statement: Sector mix shifting from 23% industrial to over 40% of revenues through FY27 post-STEAG; LSG adds aviation catering (high margin, annuity contracts till 2039)
items.quote: Post STEAG's addition into the portfolio, our sector mix will undergo a shift towards industrial vertical, which currently is at 23% to over 40% of revenues through the financial year.

items.statement: Security headcount crossed 24,900 (added ~900 in Q1); total workforce 97,000 (+3,300 QoQ); crossed 100,000 in July; no headcount target, focus on revenue/EBITDA guidance
items.quote: Our overall workforce stands today at 97,000, a growth of 3,300 quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Facility & Food margin held at 4.6% despite higher LPG prices; effective cost management and reduction of low-margin clients offset inflation
items.quote: Despite seasonality and impact of higher LPG prices playing out during the quarter, the EBITDA grew 25% year-on-year to INR 24 crores, and EBITDA margins held steady at 4.6%.

items.statement: Foundit EBITDA loss INR14 crores in Q1; full-year burn guided at INR30-35 crores (CFO) / INR35-40 crores (CEO); target Q4 FY27 breakeven at INR38-40 crores quarterly sales with INR32-33 crores cost base
items.quote: We expect the EBITDA burn for the financial year to be in the range of INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

items.statement: Foundit sales INR25 crores in Q1 (flat QoQ, 50% YoY); B2B core up 80% YoY; revenue INR19 crores; deferred revenue model with 15-18% sales-to-revenue conversion per quarter
items.quote: The business recorded a sales of INR25 crores as compared to INR26 crores in the previous quarter. This converts into a revenues of INR19 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: ELI scheme benefits insignificant so far; awaiting government clarifications; no material impact on results
items.quote: On, macro levels and ELI scheme, we've not seen any significant benefit accruing to Bluspring so far.

items.statement: Security Q1 margin dip due to higher ECL from delayed PO renewals and collections; expected recovery in Q2-Q3
items.quote: Q1 historically has been a poor quarter from a collection standpoint, because most of these POs go under renewal, the clients go through their SAP renewals of the POs, and this leads to bit of a delayed billing and delayed collection, eventually leading to higher ECL charges in quarter one.

items.statement: Top 30 clients <50% of revenue; STEAG contracts are outcome-based end-to-end O&M for large power plants; cross-selling across Bluspring services (security, FM, engineering) within large deals
items.quote: We continue to have a well-diversified client base and sector base, with top 30 clients contributing to less than 50% of our revenues.

items.statement: FM and security highly commoditized, compete with large national/international players; STEAG/Hofincons differentiated by German technical expertise, superior quality, outcome-based model enabling larger, higher-margin deals
items.quote: For most of our services, we probably would come in the top 3 in the country in terms of scale, size, service quality.

items.statement: Zero on-job fatalities in Q1; 5,000+ health & safety training hours in Smart Infra vertical; independent leadership teams for each business with board oversight
items.quote: For us, employees' well-being and safety remains paramount. We continue to report zero on-job fatalities in this quarter.

items.statement: STEAG has small operations in Middle East and one African country; potential to expand gas-based power plant O&M overseas; international revenue share could lift blended margins toward 6%
items.quote: STEAG has also done as part of a German subsidiary some very large gas-based power plants, both in India and in Middle East, and that one business vertical within STEAG, which is further something which I think we can expand gradually.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guidance ~22% for FY27 (statutory 25% with 80JJAA and Chapter VI-A deductions); quarterly variance due to deferred tax assets
items.quote: The guidance to the market, I have always told, the ETR you should consider close to around 22% for the entire year.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31
items.quote: We continue to retain our guidance of consolidated and Adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28, and ₹1,000 crores in adjusted EBITDA by FY31.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; revenue grew 44% YoY to ₹528 crore; total orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, Q1 NTV grew 42% year-on-year to reach ₹1,465 crore, and revenue grew 44% year-on-year to reach ₹528 crore. Total orders reached 13.2 million, which is up 79% year-on-year.

items.statement: Added ~1.2 million new customers in Q1 FY27, crossing one million for the first time in a quarter; annual transacting user base grew to 9.3 million
items.quote: We also added around 1.2 million new customers, crossing the one-million mark for the first time in a quarter, and our annual transacting user base grew to 9.3 million.

items.statement: International business NTV grew 76% YoY to ₹237 crore with profitable growth in UAE, Singapore and Saudi JV
items.quote: NTV grew 76% to reach ₹237 crore. Both UAE and Singapore delivered profitable growth. Our JV in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia also grew very well with margin.

items.statement: Native NTV grew 51% YoY to ₹119 crore; net revenue grew 60% YoY to ₹95 crore; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to (7.3)% of NTV from (11.4)% YoY
items.quote: Native continues to demonstrate strong growth with improving margins. NTV grew 51% year-on-year to reach ₹119 crores, and net revenue grew 60% year-on-year to reach ₹95 crores. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to (7.3)% of NTV from (11.4)% a year back, so an improvement of 410 basis points.

items.statement: InstaHelp delivered 3.82 million orders, up 43% QoQ; adjusted EBITDA loss ₹132 crore; loss per order improved from ₹447 in Q4 to ₹346
items.quote: We delivered 3.82 million orders, up 43% quarter-on-quarter. The Adjusted EBITDA loss was ₹(132) crores. Loss per order improved from ₹(447) in Q4 to ₹(346) in this quarter as micro-market density built up.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss ₹65 crore driven by InstaHelp loss of ₹132 crore; ex-InstaHelp operations delivered adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹67 crore, up 116% YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA loss stood at ₹(65) crores. But this was almost entirely driven by InstaHelp's loss of ₹(132) crores. Excluding InstaHelp, the rest of our operations delivered an adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹67 crores, which is more than 100% growth from the same period last year; specifically about 116%.

items.statement: Ended Q1 FY27 with ₹2,019 crore in cash and treasury investments, only ₹2 crore lower than previous quarter
items.quote: We ended the quarter with ₹2,019 crores in cash and treasury investments on our balance sheet which is only about ₹2 crores lower than where we ended the last quarter.

items.statement: Long-term guidance for India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp is 9-10% adjusted EBITDA margin as percentage of NTV; currently at 6.9%
items.quote: Our long-term guidance of this business was 9-10% adjusted EBITDA margin as a percentage of NTV. And this quarter, we've already demonstrated that we are at 6.9%.

items.statement: InstaHelp addressable market in top 15 cities estimated at ₹7,000-12,000 crore NTV annually; base case ₹7,000-8,000 crore, bull case ₹10,000-12,000 crore
items.quote: We believe the addressable market in the top 15 cities ranges anywhere from ₹7,000 to ₹12,000 crores NTV annually.

items.statement: InstaHelp expected to break even by FY31; no intention to make money from this business over next 5 years; margin profile likely low single-digit
items.quote: We certainly have no intentions of making any money from this business over the next 5 years, and our assumption is this business has to break even by FY31. We'd be happy if it gets there.

items.statement: InstaHelp investment level evaluated quarter-on-quarter based on market view, competitive intensity and size of prize; will continue to take investments over next 2 years or longer
items.quote: InstaHelp, fair to say over the next 2 years, if not longer, will continue to take investments. InstaHelp, we are evaluating quarter on quarter what is the right level of investment.

items.statement: UC Instant rolled out across core services (Salon, Cleaning, AC Repair, Electrician, Plumber, Carpenter) with 30-60 minute fulfillment times
items.quote: This has allowed us, through the last two quarters, to roll out UC Instant, which is basically getting all our core services, be it Salon, Cleaning, AC Repair, Electrician's Plumber, Carpenter, etc, etc, between 30 to 60 minutes.

items.statement: Water purifier filter renewal rate ~75% for early cohorts completing first replacement cycle, adding recurring higher-margin revenue stream
items.quote: As our early water-purifier cohorts complete their first replacement cycle, about 75% of them are renewing filters through us, which adds a recurring, higher-margin revenue stream.

items.statement: All three InstaHelp players limiting coverage to ~3.5-4 million households; investment going into artificially subsidising repeat user orders rather than expanding coverage
items.quote: If you actually look at the actions of the 3 players in the market over the past 6 months, actually, all of us have limited ourselves to micro-markets where the household coverage that we are covering today is only about 3.5 to 4 million households.

items.statement: No plans to enter new international markets; focus on deepening penetration in India, UAE, Singapore and Saudi JV due to management bandwidth and large opportunity size
items.quote: I don't see us entering any new international markets. I think we are focused on India, and focused on deepening our penetration in India, and I think that'll be where most of the effort will go.

items.statement: Native has line of sight to profitability over next few quarters; incremental capital required until cash generation not substantial
items.quote: Coming to Native, I think Native has done exceptionally well in terms of growth and margin improvement. Again, something similar, I would say, for Native, where we now have line of sight of profitability in Native, over the next few quarters.

items.statement: India Consumer Services margins have spikiness in AMJ and OND quarters; best visualised yearly; delivered 170 bps YoY improvement in adjusted EBITDA margin
items.quote: Our margins in this business tend to have a certain spikiness in the AMJ quarter, as well as in the OND quarter. And therefore, margins are best visualised yearly. Year on year also, the business has delivered a very healthy 170 basis points improvement in Adjusted EBITDA margin.

items.statement: India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp growth accelerated for fourth straight quarter: 10% → 19% → 21% → 26% → 29% YoY NTV growth
items.quote: This is the fourth straight quarter of acceleration, up from 10% same time last year to 19% to 21% to 26% to now 29% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: International business constant currency growth 58% YoY excluding currency impact
items.quote: Even if I remove the currency impact, it's a very healthy 58% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: InstaHelp pricing currently subsidised; full potential pricing at ₹200-300 per hour; player with disproportionate TAM share will see least volume correction when pricing normalises
items.quote: The bull case assumption that we've given here of 10,000 to 12,000 crores is actually a bull case. And we're not being conservative in this range of TAM. Our base case assumption is 7,000 to 8,000, and the aggressive assumption is 10 to 12,000.

items.statement: Management bandwidth fully occupied with India opportunity and existing international markets (UAE, Singapore, Saudi JV); no bandwidth for new geographies
items.quote: Purely from a management bandwidth standpoint, we have our hands full. With the India business opportunity, as well as actually doing justice to the opportunity, in UAE, Singapore, and the JV in Saudi.

items.statement: InstaHelp business expected to break even by FY31; no intention to make money from it over next 5 years
items.quote: We certainly have no intentions of making any money from this business over the next 5 years, and our assumption is this business has to break even by FY31.

items.statement: InstaHelp steady-state margin profile expected to be low single-digit, well below India Consumer Services
items.quote: We've also articulated that we don't think the margin profile of this business, given everything we understand of it, will reach anywhere close to India Consumer Services. It will be, in all likelihood, a low single-digit category.

items.statement: InstaHelp AOV needs to reach ₹300 for breakeven; sustainable service professional pay ₹130-160/hour
items.quote: We've articulated that the AOV has to get to around ₹300 for this business to break even and let me explain why. Today, on an average, our view is that, sustainably the service professional has to be paid about anywhere between 130 and 160 rupees per hour.

items.statement: InstaHelp frequency currently 30-40 transactions annually at compressed AOVs; future cohorts may deteriorate; 3 transactions/month at corrected pricing for 10-12M households would be home run
items.quote: the 30 to 40 transactions in a month is data that we're seeing right now at highly compressed AoVs. In our experience building marketplaces and having learned from others, rarely do larger future cohorts behave better than early cohorts. Usually, the usership in future cohorts only deteriorates

items.statement: InstaHelp is winner-take-all market; trust compounds to number one player; playing to win, not to look elegant
items.quote: We think this market, like most home services, it's a winner-take-all. Trust compounds to the number one player. We don't think there's a very large, unbounded market which can support multiple winners. We want to be the eventual winner here.

items.statement: Core India services growth at 29% has some margin from low base; secular focus on healthy pace over 5-year view
items.quote: Can it grow faster than 29%? Look, I, again, would reiterate that I don't want to get ahead of ourselves. I don't want to set the wrong expectations. I think that 29% does have a little bit of, you know, margin there because of the low base last year.

items.statement: Core India services added >5 lakh annual transacting users QoQ; funnel metrics (MAUs, DAUs, MTUs) moving right; conversion rates improving with trust
items.quote: Srinath, I think we're fairly happy overall, I would say, with the pace at which both the users, transacting users has grown, in this quarter, as you rightly articulated, more than half a million, and also, you know, their spends

items.statement: India Consumer Services marketing spend flat YoY at ₹25 crore vs ₹24 crore; better ROI on spends driving growth
items.quote: In fact, seeing year on year, in the India Consumer Services business, the marketing spends, same period last year were ₹24 crores, and this year they've been ₹25 crores. So actually, more or less flat marketing, but we've been getting a lot better ROI for our spends there.

items.statement: Beauty segment resurgence driven by supply quality improvement, retraining, mobility program (majority now have two-wheelers), and assortment expansion (Japanese facials, Forest Essentials Ayurvedic line)
items.quote: We've been driving a mobility program as well to make sure that all our service professionals in the beauty space, most of them are women, have access to a two-wheeler. A minority of our professionals had two-wheelers about a year back, today, that number is a majority.

items.statement: Core training infrastructure well-oiled for next few quarters; InstaHelp training capacity all hands on deck, focusing on efficacy and ROI not just scale
items.quote: On InstaHelp, I think it's all hands on deck right now. The pace of supply addition has been very high, and consequently, keeping pace with our training infrastructure and our trainer capacity, and making sure that our training efficacy also improves

items.statement: Native launched M3 water purifier (3-year no service, stainless steel tank, adaptive mineralizer) and Lock Ultra (inbuilt camera, auto-unlock, lurker alert); both premium, high-rated
items.quote: With M3, we are now launching a 3-year, no service needed. Very high quality machine with a stainless steel tank, adaptive mineralizer and pH balancer, etc, etc.

items.statement: Native may enter one more category over next 5 years; focus on deepening water purifiers and smart locks; not building consumer durables company
items.quote: If at all we have to venture into another category over the next 5 years, maybe we will enter one more category. But that's about it. We don't want to proliferate too much.

items.statement: Native strategy: serve underserved premium segment overlapping with Urban Company's 9.3M annual transacting users; capture disproportionate profit pool via tech-first products adjacent to core services
items.quote: We have 9.3 million annual transacting users. These represent the top 9.3 million households, or whatever, 8 million households in the country and we want to serve them more deeply through Native as an extension of our core services.

items.statement: AI deployed across support, supply onboarding, training, quality audits (proof-of-work), fraud detection (>90-95% code AI-written), marketing, finance, HR; early in leveraging full benefits
items.quote: More than 90-95% of our code now is written by AI, and we are seeing a lot of leverage in our engineering costs and headcount therein.

items.statement: AI benefits starting to show in margins but long way to go; primary goal is healthier marketplace and better service quality, not just cost efficiency
items.quote: In terms of, you know, back to margins, I think we've started to show up. But there's a long way to go. And we are also thinking about AI not just from an efficiency and cost improvement lever, but more importantly, as a lever, that can help make our marketplace significantly healthier

items.statement: Revised FY27 volume growth guidance: EXIM 15%, Domestic 25%, Overall 18%
items.quote: So, at this point of time, now I am going to revise my guidance for this financial year. Revised guidance will be EXIM will be 15%, domestic will be 25%, overall guidance will be 18% for this financial year.

items.statement: Q1 throughput all-time high at 1.4 million TEUs, up 9% YoY; EXIM up 9.8%, Domestic up 6.2%
items.quote: I am glad to announce that the Board of Directors have declared a dividend of INR 1.60 per share, that is 32% on par value of INR 5, and the throughput of the company was all-time high for any first quarter Q1, that was 1.4 million TEUs, registering a growth of 9% year-on-year, in which EXIM's contribution was 9.8% growth, domestic was 6.2% growth.

items.statement: Market share increased: EXIM +90 bps to 54%, Domestic +370 bps to 58.7%, Overall +160 bps to 55.2%
items.quote: In EXIM, it has increased by 90 basis points. In domestic, it has increased by 370 basis points. And overall increase in market share is 160 basis points, despite increase in margins also.

items.statement: Q1 capex INR 118 crore; FY27 budget INR 945 crore kept intact, may revisit after Q2
items.quote: CAPEX, we have achieved around INR 118 crores. So, as per the budget for this financial year, INR 945 crores… I would like to keep it intact. Maybe after Q2, we will revisit the budget, whether to increase it or not.

items.statement: JNPT market share rose to 62.6% from 58% YoY; Mundra share dipped to 34% from 36%; Pipavav flat at 48.2%
items.quote: In JNPT, for Q1, rail coefficient was 14.13%, and our market share was 62.6%, last year, rail coefficient was 15.5%, market share was 58%. So, there is a big growth in market share in JNPT. At Mundra, last year, the rail coefficient was 24.7%, this year it is 24.5%, almost same, but our market share has slightly dipped from 36% to 34%. In Pipavav, the rail coefficient is same, 55%, market share is

items.statement: First-mile/last-mile coverage increased from 10% (3 years ago) to 46% (end FY26); target 80% by FY27 end, 100% by FY28
items.quote: The thing is that three years back, we were having only 10% cargo that we were able to give first mile, last mile to our customers. Till end of FY26, this number has gone up to 46%. So, 46% cargo, we are able to give service to our customers for first mile, last mile. For rest 54%, customers are arranging the first mile, last mile movement themselves. Now, for this FY27, we have set up a target of

items.statement: LLF cost up 7% annually; surrendering unneeded terminals continuously; no major change in Q1
items.quote: The LLF already, we are having a 7% increase every year, but at the same time, and in my earlier calls also I told you, it is a continuous exercise that we are surrendering the terminals which are no longer required without sacrificing our business. So, that has been the company's policy constantly we are doing. So, in this quarter also, there is not much growth in LLF.

items.statement: Board declared dividend of INR 1.60 per share (32% on face value INR 5)
items.quote: I am glad to announce that the Board of Directors have declared a dividend of INR 1.60 per share, that is 32% on par value of INR 5.

items.statement: Chairman & MD Sanjay Swarup indicates this is his last month with CONCOR (superannuation)
items.quote: Mr. Swarup, I think this is your last month with CONCOR. It was very nice interacting with you all this while and good luck for your future endeavors, Mr. Swarup. Thanks a lot. Sanjay Swarup: Thank you very much

name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited

items.statement: Bavla oncology facility can support INR800-1,000 crores revenue at optimal utilization over next 4-5 years without major incremental capex
items.quote: The Bavla oncology facility has been designed with significant growth potential and we believe it can support revenues of INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores at optimal utilization over the next 4 to 5 years without requiring any major incremental capital expenditure.

items.statement: NRI sales ~10% of total; structural shift in Middle East NRI demand from investment to potential relocation; other NRI markets business as usual

items.statement: Cost of sales ~4% in Q1 vs peer group 5-10%; focused on quality of sales over possession-linked plans
items.quote: Even in Q1 we, our cost of sales is about 4%, thereabout.

items.quote: Our view is that in certain jurisdictions like Haryana and Karnataka, the RERA rules don't support the use of percentage completion accounting.

items.statement: Q1 operating cash flow INR399 crores, down 58% YoY; expect meaningful increase in rest of year to reach ~INR9,000 crores full year
items.quote: Operating cash flow in the first quarter stood at INR399 crores, a decline of 58%.

items.statement: Expect free cash flow breakeven in FY27 and strongly positive in FY28; net debt cap INR10,000 crores
items.quote: we do want to keep these 2 things in balance. We've already said that we would look at INR10,000 crores net debt as a cap that we would not like to exceed

items.statement: Targeting 13.5 million sq ft delivery in FY27
items.quote: We remain on track for 13.5 million square feet of delivery in the full year

items.statement: Booking value of projects reaching revenue recognition growing from INR17,000 crores (FY25-26) to INR40,000 crores in FY28 (~2.5x)
items.quote: over the last 2 years, FY25 and '26, the, the, the booking value of these projects that have reached revenue recognition is about INR17,000 crores. That's going up to INR40,000 crores

items.statement: Key risks to FY28 FCF: overshooting business development, substantial project delays, huge cost overruns from global situation worsening
items.quote: I think the only other is very substantial project delays or, you know, very huge kind of cost overrun because of the global situation worsening or things like that.

items.statement: Q2 CY2026 orders grew 50% YoY to ~INR 2,400 crores; H1 orders up 36% to INR 8,600 crores
items.quote: For Q2 2026, very important 50% growth in orders. So that's year-on-year comparable to the last year same quarter and this year and 21% on the revenue growth

items.statement: Order backlog stands at INR 11,900 crores with no slow-moving orders; 40% executable in next 2 quarters
items.quote: Backlog, strong backlog, INR11,900 crores of order backlog, in which there is no slow moving or a non-moving order. Everything you will get materialized over a period of time as scheduled with the customers

items.statement: Operational EBITA margin at 12.8% for H1; Q2 margin 12.6% vs 13.6% in Q1 due to material cost and forex headwinds
items.quote: I think when you look at EBITDA, it was 13.6%points in last quarter, and today, it is 12.6 percentage. And what we got was a scale benefit 2.1% What we lost on material cost was 3% roughly

items.statement: Two price hikes implemented in Electrification; price increases lag commodity cost inflation; flow business passing hikes, project business constrained by tenders
items.quote: At the same time, what we have done is we have passed on two price lists into the market. These are two price hikes. This is a publicly available price list, which is there

items.statement: Material cost rose to 63% of revenue from 61% in Q1 due to copper/metal price hardening and forex volatility
items.quote: material cost was 63% roughly compared to 61% last quarter, and 60% in the Q1 2025. So we have a bridge profit walk, which we will take you through

items.statement: Strong orders from data centers (15-17%), metals & mining (15%), oil & gas (9%), buildings & infra (8%), renewables (6%); commercial buildings and data centers driving faster decisions
items.quote: Data Centers orders in this quarter has been almost 15% to 17% of our orders came from base orders. Metals and Mining was 15 %and then oil and gas was 9% and Buildings and Infra was 8%. Renewables was 6%

items.statement: Investing USD 75-80 million in capacity expansion targeting 15-20% sales headroom; new Nelamangala factory launched for data center products
items.quote: We are investing quite heavily in increasing our capacity, because we are definitely seeing that picking up which will come -- the demand will multifold in the coming quarters and maybe like 2027, 2028

items.statement: Manufacturing locations increased from 5 to 6 with Nelamangala second site; capacity utilization targeted at 80-85% with 15% headroom
items.quote: Now the number of manufacturing locations has increased from 5 to 6 because we had Nelamangala, our second location which has been added so that's why the 6 locations

items.statement: Export share declined to 13% in Q2 from 17% in Q1 due to West Asia crisis impact; forex volatility affecting margins
items.quote: And in terms of geography, you could look at it, we have just 13% in exports for the quarter compared to 17% what we did in the previous quarter at the same time

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 90 per share declared including robotics divestment proceeds and 50% payout ratio
items.quote: we did declare an interim dividend of INR90 per share, which includes the proceeds which we got from the divestment of robotics plus a 50% payout ratio of what we do from the normal earnings per share

items.statement: T.K. Sridhar designated MD from Jan 1, 2027; CFO search underway to complete in next couple months
items.quote: In the month of May, the Board accorded him the status as the MD, Managing Director Designate, starting from 1st of January 2027. So now between now and end of the year, I am preparing the transition

items.statement: QCO compliance progressing with government extensions on some components; local supplier base and factories enabling compliance
items.quote: And also, there is some of the relaxation which is coming from the government on some of the components and equipment where they have postponed and given an extended time for us to meet those requirements

items.statement: Electrification orders up 77% YoY with backlog at INR 4,800-4,900 crores; Motion orders up 26% QoQ with backlog at INR 4,900 crores; Automation revenue INR 524 crores (7% up) with 30% services mix
items.quote: orders for electrification, the strongest growing segment we see for the quarter, 77% up on orders, and orders again from data centers, metals and mining, infra, cement sectors. We have a strong backlog, which is also today at INR4,800 crores, INR 4,900 crores, for EL, electrification segment

items.statement: Elevated commodity prices and rupee depreciation expected to persist; not comfortable guiding mid-teens EBITDA margin; focus on protecting current margins
items.quote: I know I'm 100% sure that you have all this information. But just to basically sensitize, this is a topic which we will have to continue to deal with in the next few quarters to come. So elevated commodity prices and continued rupee depreciation will be extended as what our research says

items.statement: Short-term outlook: government capex pickup, private consumption, manufacturing base to drive growth; geopolitical uncertainty and subnormal monsoon as risks for next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So this is more a bit of a short-term outlook, what we see because today, with the rapid changes which is happening, I think the short term is more reliable or I think something which we could look at it rather than even medium term as well

items.statement: Revenue growth aspiration of 20-25% long-term
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter grew 27% Y-o-Y, ahead of our long-term growth aspiration of 20-25%.

items.statement: Store addition guidance of more than 30 stores for FY27
items.quote: We have been adding around 30 stores -- not less than 30 stores every year. And again, I have already told in the earnings call that we'll be definitely doing more than 30 stores this year also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 8-10% for the year
items.quote: We have already given the guidance that our EBITDA margin will be between 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to be between 15% and 16% going forward
items.quote: So, going ahead, I'd say that we'll definitely be between 15% and 16%.

items.statement: Healthy demand across key product categories drove 27% revenue growth
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter grew 27% Y-o-Y, ahead of our long-term growth aspiration of 20-25%, driven by continued market share gains, healthy demand across key product categories, and the contribution from our expanding store network.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps to 10.4% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR124 crore s, while EBITDA margin expanded by nearly 90 basis points to 10.4

items.statement: PAT margin improved 61 bps to 6.5% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Profit after tax grew 40% year -on-year to INR77 crore s, with PAT margin improving by 61 basis points to 6.5

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 75 bps to 16.1% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Gross margin remained healthy at 16.1%, expanding by approximately 75 basis points compared to the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 18% for Q1 FY27, continuing for three quarters
items.quote: Same-store sales growth for quarter 1 stood at 18%. We also witnessed a reduction in inventory by INR177 crore s compared to March 2026

items.statement: Opened 3 new stores in Q1 FY27, total network at 210 stores
items.quote: During the quarter, we opened three new stores. Our network has expanded to 210 stores as on date.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by INR177 crore to INR663 crore; working capital loan reduced to INR175 crore
items.value: INR663 crore inventory, INR175 crore working capital loan
items.quote: Now the inventory stands at INR663 crores, and reduction of short-term borrowing to approximately INR175 crores as of June 30th, 2026.

items.statement: Bihar contributed 72% of Q1 revenue, UP 16%, Jharkhand 11%
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, Bihar remained our largest revenue contributor at 72% for quarter 1, followed by UP at 16% and Jharkhand at 11%.

items.statement: Market share gains continued despite challenging conditions
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that Aditya Vision has delivered another quarter of strong, profitable and market share-led growth despite challenging conditions.

items.statement: Government appeal to avoid gold and import-dependent products affected sentiment
items.quote: The appeal from government to desist from buying gold and other import dependent products further casted gloom over our customers' buying sentiments.

items.statement: Working capital loan reduced to INR175 crore as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Inventory stood at INR663 crores as of June 30, 2026, while working capital loan reduced to INR175 crore s, reflecting efficient inventory management, healthy operating cash flows and continued liquidity -prioritized balance sheet discipline

items.statement: Board approved appointment of MSKA & Associates LLP as statutory auditor
items.quote: In line with our commitment to the highest standards of corporate governance, the Board has approved the appointment of MSKA & Associates LLP, Chartered Accountants, one of India's leading audit firms and an independent m ember firm of the BDO International network, as our statutory auditor

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 18% for Q1 FY27
items.quote: Same-store sales growth for quarter 1 stood at 18%.

items.quote: CDSL has opened about 58 lakh new demat accounts during the quarter, taking the total demat accounts on the CDSL platform to 18.59 crores as on 30th June 2026 and maintaining a market share of approximately 80%.

items.statement: Board and shareholders approved appointment of Shri Amit Mahajan as Executive Director Vertical 1 and Srimati Nayana Ovalekar as Executive Director Vertical 2 after SEBI approval
items.quote: During the quarter, our governing Board and our shareholders have approved the appointment of Shri Amit Mahajan as Executive Director, Vertical 1; and Srimati Nayana Ovalekar as Executive Director for Vertical 2.

items.statement: Standalone income INR327 crores, standalone net profit INR144 crores for Q1 FY27
items.value: Income INR327 crores; Net profit INR144 crores
items.quote: Coming to our financial performance, CDSL reported a stand-alone income of INR327 crores and a stand-alone net profit of INR144 crores for Q1 of FY '26, '27.

items.statement: Consolidated total income INR341 crores, consolidated net profit INR118 crores for Q1 FY27
items.value: Income INR341 crores; Net profit INR118 crores
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the total income stood at INR341 crores and a net profit of INR118 crores.

items.statement: CVL revenue from operations INR45 crores, up 22% YoY; total income INR50 crores, up 18% YoY; profit before tax INR15.98 crores, down 4% YoY
items.quote: During Q1 FY '27, CVL reported revenue from operations of INR45 crores as compared to INR36 crores during the same period last year, reflecting a growth of INR8 crores or 22%.

items.statement: Impairment cost (debtors' provision) was INR2.22 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So, the impairment cost, i.e. debtors' provision is INR2.22 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Standalone net profit declined to INR144 crores from INR152 crores YoY due to lower dividend from subsidiary (INR39.5 crores vs INR62 crores)
items.value: Dividend from subsidiary INR39.5 crores vs INR62 crores

items.statement: Consolidated net profit increased to INR118 crores from INR102 crores YoY

items.statement: Folio count increased to INR38.73 crores from INR33.2 crores YoY (17% growth)
items.quote: Amit, the folio is INR38.73 crores.

items.quote: We have achieved unlisted revenue of INR0.30 crores, and application processing fees of INR2.32 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Technology expenses stabilized this quarter; management says spend depends on evolving regulatory requirements and technology changes, no forward guidance given
items.quote: So, see, the regulatory requirements keep on changing as per the needs of the market and what needs is there. Also, technology is also changing rapidly. The intent is that we have to be nimble as well as very, very active in ensuring that the best-in-class technology continues to remain active on the CDSL platform.

items.statement: ISIN issuance capability for unlisted companies not yet live; in active engagement with regulators, will announce when operational
items.quote: And in terms of the ISIN, it's again, we are in active engagement. It's not yet gone live. It needs to go through its processes. So as and when it goes live, we will definitely be making the necessary announcements.

items.statement: Unified KYC integration with CKYC in testing phase; no exact timeline given, depends on CKYC system readiness and regulatory discussions
items.quote: So far as unified KYC is concerned, we are in the process of getting integrated with CKYC. And we are in the process of testing their systems. That will happen, but, I cannot give you an exact date.

items.quote: We've seen a considerable drop in the second and third month. We are waiting for it to stabilize to have a fair idea. Earlier people were doing searches for 1 PAN multiple times a day, which has come down significantly.

items.quote: So, breakup of other income consists of consolidated account statement related fee, which is around INR14.80 crores, e-voting income of INR6.32 crores, Investment-mark-to-market related gain and other income accrued on investment is INR43.8 crores.

items.statement: Investment portfolio primarily in debt schemes; 5-7% in ETFs; no direct equity mutual fund investments
items.quote: We do not make any direct investment in the equity schemes of mutual fund. We generally invest in debt schemes. We have a small portion of ETF investment, which ranges from 5% to 7% of our investable portfolio.

items.statement: Margin pledge income INR6.19 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Margin Pledge income in this quarter is INR6.19 crores.

items.statement: Employee costs up 30% QoQ due to year-end appraisal cycle and variable pay; headcount increased YoY with operational scale
items.quote: year-on-year has increased with the number of employees have grown. And that is a function of as the complexity and the scale of operations grow and whatever is required, we are very mindful of that

items.statement: Management does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance; no forward-looking statements on technology spend, KYC revenue run-rate, or unified KYC timeline
items.quote: CDSL does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance. Anything said on this call, which reflects CDSL's outlook for the future, or which could be constituted as forward-looking statements, must be reviewed in conjunction with the risks that the company faces.

items.statement: Incremental demat market share declined ~420 bps since March 2026 to 81.4% in June 2026; management focuses on long-term value proposition over quarterly share
items.quote: I think, again, I'll repeat what I said in the the reply to the first question, we are an infrastructure company. And our intent at least CDSL is not a quarter-on-quarter growth. It is a long-term sustainable growth, which creates value proposition for the market.

items.statement: CVL income purely KYC-related; Search API revenue included in overall KRA income but not separately quantified; higher fetch volumes offset pricing reduction
items.quote: It is part of the online data charges that we normally provide as a disclosure.

items.statement: Consolidated total income INR340.50 crores vs INR295.14 crores YoY; consolidated net profit INR118 crores vs INR102 crores YoY
items.value: Income INR340.50 crores; Net profit INR118 crores
