items.statement: KYC rack rate reduction impact partially offset by higher fetch volumes and new Search API revenue (INR0.25 per search)
items.quote: Further, when the charges were reduced by SEBI, they had allowed us to charge on the Search API, which again gave us some revenue, which reduced the overall impact.

items.statement: Unlisted issuer revenue dropped sharply to INR0.30 crores from INR3.5 crores QoQ; management says driven by regulatory intent to bring more companies into depository fold
items.quote: See, again, it's difficult to give a forward-looking statement, but it is all driven by overall regulatory intent of ensuring that more and more companies come into the fold of depositories.

items.statement: E-commerce revenue grew over 10% YoY; ground B2B grew ~14% YoY; air volume growth ~2.6%, ground volume growth ~9%
items.quote: This quarter versus last year, e-commerce would have grown by about from revenue point of view, more than 10%.

items.statement: Auto sector growing in high teens within surface B2B segment
items.quote: We see more growth from auto point of view in the surface B2B, which as a segment has been growing in high teens consistently in the last few years.

items.statement: Yield improvement driven by general price increases, targeted corrections on loss-making lanes/customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through
items.quote: There has been a good amount of growth in the -- from pricing from RPK, RPS point of view. The actions that we had taken for improving our yield in terms of looking at the loss-making lanes or loss-making customers in some of the products.

items.statement: Fuel surcharge auto-adjusts monthly; diesel surcharge revised from June after May price hike; air fuel surcharge rose from April with Brent
items.quote: prices for customers would have gone up because of this surcharge going up especially after the month of May

items.statement: Targeting stable, consistent margin improvement through efficiency and yield; Q2 challenge is flexing resources with peak volumes
items.quote: We look at having a stable, consistent improvement in the margins, and we'll work towards that unless, of course, there is a plan that we come to the market in terms of any major expansion we have to plan.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 70% B2B / 30% B2C; 60% air / 40% ground; weight mix 1:3 air:ground (25% air, 75% ground)
items.quote: In terms of revenue, it remains at around 70%-30%, 70% being B2B and 30% being B2C, or 2% plus/minus.

items.statement: BFSI (documents & cards) 10-15% of revenue; total documents/small parcels ~25-30%; BFSI stagnant due to elongated card cycles
items.quote: Documents and card, especially the BFSI segment would be between 10% to 15% of total revenue.

items.statement: E-commerce shipments >50 million (50%+ of 96.15M total); 3PL e-com market share ~12-13%; SME share stable, slight gain
items.quote: E-com will be 50-plus million in this.

items.statement: Freighter pallet utilization 85-90%; network continuously optimized; 2 acquired aircraft integrated; can add daytime flights if yield supports
items.quote: We measure freighter utilization in terms of the pallet utilization that remains between 85% to 90%.

items.statement: Standalone capex INR 100-150 cr/year (replacement + small expansion); aviation capex varies with engine/maintenance cycles; new hubs planned in South (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai over next few quarters
items.quote: the annualized capex may remain to the tune of INR100 crores to INR150 crores for the stand-alone.

items.statement: Belly cargo 30-40% of monthly load (up to 70-80% on weekends); 8 own-aircraft stations + 25-50 belly cargo locations
items.quote: Belly cargo typically moves between 30% to 40% of our overall load, including both the stations at which our own aircraft, there are currently 8 stations on Blue Dart flight flies.

items.statement: Air: market leader; surface B2B & e-com: growing share, aiming to lead; e-com pricing competitive, Blue Dart positioned as premium
items.quote: In air, we would be the market leader, whereas when it comes to surface B2B or e-commerce, this is where we are growing and trying to gain more market share to lead the market.

items.statement: Total tonnage 364,430 tons; shipments 96.15 million; volume growth 7% YoY
items.quote: Total tonnage was 364,430 tons and the number of shipments was 96.15 million.

items.statement: No explicit volume or margin guidance; focus on organic growth, market share gains, and stable margin improvement
items.quote: I will go with that, Alok. I mean no, I would say, major plans of expansion to add significantly more volumes, everything that will come from marketplace, where we'll try to gain more share.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR3,000 crores for FY27 and over INR4,000 crores for FY28 with Odisha plant
items.quote: So this year, last year, our top line was around INR2,500 crores. So this year, we are expecting somewhere around INR3,000 crores. So that's what 20% up. And next year, with the new plant, we see this going up to around more than INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 15% long-term after Odisha plant stabilizes
items.quote: But otherwise, we expect the long-term margins to stay after our Odisha plant around 15%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 margins expected similar or better than Q1 FY27
items.quote: But yes, the current quarter looks to be similar or even better than what we have delivered this last quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 18.8% with spread of INR133/kg vs INR107/kg previous quarter
items.quote: Sir, again, congratulations on a great set of numbers. Sir, my question is of this 18.8% EBITDA margin, what can be attributable to this temporary cotton import duty? And more importantly, is this margin sustainable in the long run?

items.statement: Odisha plant expected to deliver 300-400 bps higher EBITDA margin than existing plants
items.quote: So about EBITDA accretion, this plant has many incentives which are embedded. So we expect the margins coming out of that plant to be at least 300 to 400 basis points or even more than what we do in our old plants.

items.statement: Odisha greenfield expansion of 150,000 spindles at INR975 crores, Phase 1 production starting Q3 FY27, full completion by FY27 end
items.quote: Our 150,000-spindle greenfield expansion project in Odisha is also progressing as planned. We are very excited with that. Construction activities is underway and the first phase of production is expected to commence during the third quarter of the current financial year and we intend to finish our whole project within this financial year.

items.statement: Odisha plant targets 90% utilization by March FY27 end, 96-97% by start of FY28
items.quote: So we plan to start commissioning the plant somewhere in the next quarter. And we expect to ramp up the whole plant. It's a big plant. So it will take us around 5 to 6 months to fully ramp up. And I think by March end, we should be at about 90% capacity utilization for the whole plant.

items.statement: Odisha plant expected to contribute 30-40% of potential revenue in Q4 FY27, full contribution from FY28
items.quote: So right now, we are not considering anything for Q3, but whatever we get will be bonus. But in Q4, we expect almost 30% to 40% of the revenues of the total potential to kick in.

items.statement: Solar power projects commenced commercial operations, expected to reduce annual power cost by 12-15% (~INR15 crores annual savings)
items.quote: The project is expected to reduce our annual power cost by approximately 12% to 15%, while simultaneously increasing the share of renewable energy in our overall power consumption.

items.statement: Order book maintained at 70-90 days consistently as risk management policy
items.quote: So we continue to see this is generally our strategy. We have an order book ranging from 70 to 90 days in any year, whether it is this year or even the last year or whichever year because this is our policy we work to manage our risk of having higher inventory. And we continue to do that.

items.statement: Healthy demand across all markets, supportive domestic outlook aided by festive season, strong export demand particularly from China
items.quote: Demand from all the markets continued to remain healthy, and we are also encouraged by the outlook going into the second quarter. On the domestic front, we expect demand to remain supportive in the coming quarters, aided by the festive season and improving consumption trends.

items.statement: China emerged as major yarn buyer (20,000 tons/month) driving global demand, Bangladesh spinning crisis boosting demand
items.quote: And out of which we make almost 400,000 tons every month, and China is just buying 20,000 tons. So it's a very small minuscule portion of Indian textile basket. So we don't expect China to go out of the system because there are some inherent advantages.

items.statement: Yarn spreads increased to INR133/kg in Q1 FY27 from INR107/kg previous quarter due to 10-11% price rise in last 90 days
items.quote: So the overall spread was INR133 vis-a-vis INR107 last quarter.

items.statement: India-UK FTA concluded, India-EU FTA progressing; expected to improve competitiveness in export markets over medium term (6-9 months for orders to materialize)
items.quote: The recently concluded India-U.K. free trade agreement and the progress towards a comprehensive India-EU trade agreement has the potential to significantly improve India's competitiveness going forward in key export markets over the medium term.

items.statement: Cotton import duty resumption on 31 Oct; company lobbying for extension, has inventory for 2 quarters so no near-term impact
items.quote: So right now, this import duty is the resumption is still 31st October. And so we have planned accordingly. And we are talking to the government to extend it. So those talks are still going on and government is listening to us.

items.statement: Odisha land allows tripling capacity; future capex dependent on balance sheet comfort
items.quote: So we have got land for we can triple our capacity at Odisha. We have that kind of land there. So rest, what we spend in the future in next 2, 3 years will depend solely on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Acquisition of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales (fabric/garment) under progress, expected to close in ~1 quarter, INR250 crores revenue from FY28
items.quote: Well, that is still under progress. Unfortunately, it's taking a little more time than what we envisaged, but I think it maybe take another 1 quarter, and we expect the full impact start coming, which will be around INR250 crores from next financial year.

items.statement: Merger to be predominantly via preferential shares, minimal cash outflow (~INR25-30 crores), no significant debt increase
items.quote: So the merger will be predominantly preferential shares. So there will be a small outflow of cash. I think it will be less than maybe around INR25 crores, INR30 crores. I think merger won't have a lot of debt involved.

items.statement: Slight shift to more blends and different counts, but no major product mix change; value-added definition varies
items.quote: So the definition of value add is very different for everyone. So there has been a slight shift not in the product mix, but maybe different blends. We are running more blends. items.statement: Export mix 60-70% to China and Bangladesh, rest diversified; client addition/subtraction ongoing daily
items.quote: So 60% to 70% of our export is to these 2 countries and rest is divided between many countries. So we have a similar kind of exposure as our country has for exports.

items.statement: US indirect exposure via vendors doubling offtake in last 6 months; no direct US exports
items.quote: So we don't export anything to U.S. directly. But we have seen a lot of our vendors who export to U.S., Their lifting has gone up in the last 6 months. So we see a clear trend of those customers who were not buying initially or buying very less quantity from us have almost doubled their offtake.

items.statement: Cotton inventory covered for 4-5 months, procurement cycle completed by Feb-Mar annually
items.quote: So see, generally, we procure cotton for the whole season by February, March. So that's our normal procurement cycle and which we did this year as well. And prices generally go up in this period of time, almost every year because of the end of the season. So we don't have a problem right now. We are covered for like 4, 5 months.

items.statement: No incremental debt from merger; future Odisha expansion capex dependent on balance sheet leverage comfort
items.quote: I think merger won't have a lot of debt involved. So I think there won't be any incremental increase in debt because of that.

items.statement: Odisha incentives: INR2.50/unit power subsidy, 30% capital subsidy (uncapped), land subsidy linked to employment, INR7,000/employee employment subsidy
items.quote: So we are going to get INR2.50 subsidy on the power, whatever we use. And then we have a capital subsidy of 30%. And then we have some land subsidy, which we are going to get after we have a specific number of employment. And then there is an employment subsidy, which is about INR7,000 per employee.

items.statement: Management acknowledges cyclicality, expects 18-20% margins may not sustain long-term but sees structural upward bias from consolidation, compliance advantages for large players
items.quote: And the 18%, 19%, 20% might not be sustainable in the long-term, but we expect them to be healthier than where they were in last 2, 3 years going forward next year.

items.statement: India cotton prices aligned with international markets after prolonged premium, improving spinner competitiveness
items.quote: Coming to cotton, one of the positive developments for the industry has been the alignment of Indian cotton prices with international markets after prolonged period, during which the domestic cotton traded at a meaningful premium.

items.statement: Expect to maintain PBT margins at FY26 levels on conservative basis for full year FY27
items.quote: For the full year, we are even on a conservative basis, we hold to the PBT margin of the last financial year.

items.statement: Non-GML debt repayment to be completed by end of September 2025
items.quote: Regarding the non -GML debt reduction, we are well on track to complete the repayment by end of September.

items.statement: Customs duty benefit expected to be INR 60 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: It's in the range of INR60 crores for Q2.

items.statement: Demand remains strong in July, similar to Q1 excluding Adhik-Maas impact
items.quote: The demand on ground is strong. It continues like Q1.

items.statement: Q1 consolidated PBT margin at 5.1% vs 5.5-5.6% previously due to customs duty pass-through, exchange dilution, and platinum/silver gains
items.quote: Then the PBT margins are around what, 5.1%, which was at around 5.5% -5.6% before, So the onetime gain from the customs duty, basically, if you cut it into three, Onetime gain of what INR30 crores- INR40 crore s, that we had to give back to the consumers by way of offers, et c for people to come and exchange their old gold instead of paying cash

items.statement: Exchange is margin dilutive by 0.2-0.3%; cash-for-gold is margin accretive and expected to offset dilution
items.quote: And you know that exchange itself is margin dilutive by around 0.2% -0.3%. That also has to be taken care. And then you still will remember that we had some onetime gain of plati num, silver, etc which was in the range of 0.2%.

items.statement: Employee cost increased 0.2-0.3% in Q1 due to higher increments; operating leverage expected to absorb
items.quote: And again, you would have also noticed that there has been employee cost increase, because employees are one of our key strengths, and we always take steps to nurture and retain talent, and that's also there around 0.2% -0.3% in Q1.

items.statement: Recycled gold share reached over 46% of revenue in Q1 FY27; June exceeded 55%; target 55-60% going forward
items.quote: The initiative was well received by our customers, helping us to increase the share of recycled gold as a percentage of revenue to over 46% during Q1 FY 2027. For the month of June, the share of recycled gold was in excess of 55%, and our efforts will be to maintain the share in the range of 55% to 60% g oing forward.

items.statement: Sale of two non-core land parcels for INR 102 crores; expect to conclude and receive proceeds by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: We have made considerable progress with respect to the sale of non -core real estate assets. We have signed the agreement with potential buyers for 2 separate parcels of land with an aggregate consideration amount to around INR102 crores. We expect to conclude the sale process and receive consideration before the end of the ongoing quarter.

items.statement: Franchisee FOCO model delivers ~14% ROCE for partners
items.quote: It's a margin share. And their ROCEs will be in the range of, 14%.

items.statement: Cash-for-gold gaining traction: single-digit share in Q1, moving to double digits; buys gold at discount to spot
items.quote: For the June quarter, gold for cash portion was in single digit. Now it is moving to double digits. Which is highly margin accretive when compared to exchange.

items.statement: Non-South revenue share now 50-60%; hyperlocal strategy with 30-40% local inventory, 50-60% national inventory
items.quote: Our revenue share from the non -South markets are more than what, 50% - 60% now. And Kalyan has its own USP. We are a very hyperlocal brand. We compete the local players, unorganized players and also national players because we keep 30% - 40% of inventory, which is local and 50%- 60% of inventory which is national.

items.statement: Target to become non-GML debt-free by September 2025; then release second tranche of real estate collaterals
items.quote: Regarding the non -GML debt reduction, we are well on track to complete the repayment by end of September. Post that, we will initiate steps for the release of the second tranche of real estate collaterals.

items.statement: Gold price volatility causes consumer pause of 2-3 weeks; wedding demand cannot pause longer; volumes auto-adjust to budget
items.quote: wedding demand cannot take a pause of more than what, 2 - 3 weeks because wedding has to happen. The discretionary demand, they can wait maybe a month or 1.5 months, whatever occasion they are trying to buy for

items.statement: No fixed policy on customs duty changes; passed on to consumers via exchange promotions in Q1
items.quote: It is all depends on market dynamics. So there's no policy around these kind of things. But this quarter or the last quarter because of the promotion for exchange we used that also for promoting our old gold exchange.

items.statement: Gold price correction of 15-20% not overreacted to; procurement manages product grammage at consumer sweet spot
items.quote: And the price correction has been only 15% - 20% and for which we do not overreact for these kind of things. And it's a task for procurement team, and they always keep products on the sweet spot where consumers come maximum for that so -called sweet spot.

items.statement: Candere PAT positive in Q1 FY27 (INR 2.1 cr vs loss of INR 10 cr); to remain PAT positive for FY27; adding inventory to existing stores for throughput
items.quote: Candere has been PAT positive for the first quarter and should continue for this financial year. And we told you that Candere we will be opening around 50 showrooms in the financial year. And the focus for Candere more will be to add inve ntory in the existing stores so that we get more throughput in the existing showrooms.

name: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Limited

EBITDA margin at 20.1% versus 20.27% in Quarter 1 Financial Year '26 and 19.9% in Quarter 4 Financial Year '26.

items.statement: QIP raised INR 1,500 crore oversubscribed; INR 1,100 crore used to reduce debt; promoter preferential allotment INR 600 crore with 25% upfront
items.quote: The QIP successfully raised INR 1,500 crores and has oversubscribed, demonstrating the deep trust and confidence of institutional investors in the vision of your company. The government receivables are coming on time to a certain extent. So that risk, to a certain extent, is mitigated. Loss funding had got reduced a bit in last quarter.

items.statement: Kondapur old hospital rental cost INR 90 lakh/month + GST plus INR 3-4 crore operating costs; to be shut in ~6 months

Rahul Jeewani: So, annual cost of maybe around INR 12 crore. Abhinay Bollineni: Towards the rental, and you can assume another INR 3 crore-INR 4 crore towards the operational expense in sustaining that hospital

items.statement: Maharashtra ramp-up slower than South due to doctor alignment challenges (part-time to full-time transition); Nagpur now at INR 30 crore/month revenue after 18-24 month maturation
items.quote: One key difference between Maharashtra and South is, I think the South ideology of full-time practice is lot more easier to get aligned with doctors. items.statement: Common empanelment (JIC) process creating uncertainty; insurance companies and JIC gaining clarity; expected to settle in next few months

I think now insurance companies are also getting clarity on the way forward from JIC, and JIC itself is taking some stands and making some changes. I think it will settle down now. Over the next few months, things should settle down.

items.statement: Doctor hiring for FY27 largely done in Bangalore; continuous hiring as hospitals mature; Maharashtra doctor alignment slower due to practice model differences
items.quote: Doctor hiring is never completed fully. For that year, we are done. I think for this financial year we are sorted. We still will keep adding more and more doctors as the hospital matures.

items.quote: we have kept a target for us to do a 35% plus for the whole year

items.quote: it is a onetime write-off of a government client. Now has it -- because of that, the impact has been almost like an INR4 crores. But the net effect of that is only INR80 lakhs as far as the P&L is concerned

items.quote: we remain highly confident of deli vering meaningful growth in FY27. We expect the next quarter to be stronger with higher revenue with robust EBITDA margins

items.quote: A key milestone during the quarter was the signing of long-term supply agreement with FACC Austria, a leading aerospace Tier-1 supplier. The agreement carries an initial value of USD7.5 million over a five-year period with opportunities for scope expansion over time.

items.quote: Accordingly, our overall gross block by end of FY27 is expected to be approximately double the current value, primarily driven by Saudi JV investment. We are in the process to infuse approximately US$10 million into JV expected to happen during this month.

items.statement: Additional capacity investment being advanced earlier than planned as qualification programs convert to serial production
items.quote: As these qualification programs convert into serial production, we will need to invest early in expanding capacity to support future demand. items.quote: For finance, our manufacturing facility are currently operating approximately 58% utilization. items.statement: Strong customer procurement behaviour and sustained demand across core business; tooling demand visibility constructive for next quarter
items.quote: This momentum is being driven by strong customer procurement behaviour, sustained demand across our core business, and the early benefits of the strategic investments we have made in the past quarters, which are now beginning to translate into tangible business opportunities and customer engagements.

items.statement: Revenue mix: aero tooling 76%, precision components and assembly 24% (including Hobel 21%); H2 FY27 expected heavier PCA-led contribution
items.quote: From a revenue mix perspective, aero tooling contributed approximately 76% of total revenue. The balance came from our precision component and assembly businesses, which includes nuclear, semiconductor, aerospace segments, and Hobel Bellows. Within this, Hobel contributed 21% of total revenue.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crores via QIP for MPS compliance and strategic flexibility; not immediate fundraising
items.quote: So, what we have in place is a board resolution which to raise up to INR750 crores. So, the objective for this initiation is, I would like to call it, this is primarily to provide flexibility as we work towards the achieving of our minimum public shareholding, which is due in the next 18 months.

items.statement: Asset turn currently slightly over 2x; expected 2.5-3x over 2-3 years as utilization improves; ROCE ~15-16% currently, could reach 20-21%+
items.quote: Historically, aero tooling as a segment has always provided a better asset turns. However, since we are moving aggressively into the precision component side, there we expect a two times of asset turns. So, hence, on a two to three year basis, we can expect asset turns roughly between a 2.5% to 3% or more likely closer to a two and a half times to say so.

items.statement: Saudi JV with Kanoo Group progressing per plan; facility setup, equipment deployment, leadership hiring underway; customer engagement encouraging
items.quote: Work relating to the facility, equipment deployment, leadership hiring continues in line with our implementation plan. During the quarter, we also met with several prospective customers to update them on the progress of the venture and the manufacturing capabilities being established.

items.statement: Free trade warehousing zone fully operational to mitigate tariff disruptions; monitoring further developments
items.quote: On tariffs, as we have indicated, free trade warehousing zone has strengthened our ability to mitigate tariff-related disruptions and provide customers with greater flexibility in managing delivery schedules. However, we remain watchful on any further

items.quote: Employee cost stood at 15% of revenue with a total of 1,232 employees, while operating expenses were 13% of revenue, both reflecting some benefits of operating leverage as revenue continued to scale.

items.statement: Potential US tariffs on India being monitored; mitigants include free trade warehouse, European customer diversification, and Saudi manufacturing footprint
items.quote: And then if you see the newer engagements that we are having, including the FCC agreement, has been largely with European customers and we continue to do that. And there's obviously Saudi Arabia, where we are setting up the manufacturing footprint, which hedges these kinds of risks.

items.statement: Dheya Engineering (micro gas turbine) selected in top 100 deep-tech companies; part of PM delegation to France; targeting USD10 million raise with Unimich participation
items.quote: Dheya is also looking to raise approximately USD10 million through a combination of equity and debt, including potential funding support from the Technology Development Board. Unimech intends to participate in the equity

items.quote: Other incomes for the quarter stood at INR7 crores, approximately half the level reported in the previous quarter, primarily because a significant portion of our treasury surplus was deployed towards the acquisition of Hobel Bellows.

items.statement: Global OEMs increasingly shifting manufacturing outsourcing to India; robust pipeline of business opportunities; leap engine demand by Indian airline reinforces long-term growth
items.quote: Additionally, global OEMs are increasingly shifting and expanding their manufacturing outsourcing to the Indian manufacturing ecosystem, resulting in robust pipeline of business opportunities. We believe Unimech is well-positioned to benefit from these structural industry trends.

items.statement: Unimech positioned as preferred partner for global OEMs/Tier-1s due to engineering capability, customer credibility, and access to capital
items.quote: The combination of advanced manufacturing capabilities, customer credibility, and access to capital is not widely available. We believe this positions Unimech well to become a scaling partner for global OEMs and Tier -1 suppliers as they diversify their sup ply chains and expand their manufacturing requirements

items.statement: Subcontracting cost low at ~3% of revenue reflecting focus on in-house capability utilization
items.quote: Subcontracting cost remained low at approximately 3% of revenue, reflecting our continued focus on maximizing in-house capability utilization.

items.statement: Hobel engaging with 2 new customers in locomotive and power generation; technical evaluations and commercial submissions underway; onboarding expected by end FY27
items.quote: In addition, discussions with two new customers in the locomotive and power generation industry respectively are progressing very well with technical evaluations and commercial submissions are currently underway. Subject to successful qualification, we expect both customers to be onboarded by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth 10-15% over FY26 base; EBITDA per ton INR7,500-8,500; volume growth 10-15% over FY26
items.quote: In terms of overall 2027 numbers that you have been asking is we believe we will be very much comfortable achieving the EBITDA margin per ton in the range of INR 7,500 to INR 8,500, with again the revenue growth of 10% to 15% over the base of 2026 and EBITDA growth of again 10% to 15% over 2026 number.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance INR7,500-8,500; target to maintain Q1 sales volume
items.quote: Secondly, in t erms of Q2, we believe our EBITDA margin will be in terms of INR7,500 to INR8,500, so that is the range we would like to give for Q2 numbers. And in terms of volume, we will try our best to achieve the current Q1 sales volume number in Q2 also

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance ~12% (+/-1-2%); PAT margin guidance ~6% (+/-1%)
items.quote: Secondly, in terms of margin, for FY27, we would give a margin guidance of around 12% with a deviation or standard deviation of 1% or 2%. In terms of PAT, we want to give a guidance of 6% with a standard deviation of 1%.

items.statement: Kesda Phase 1 capex INR930 cr mostly deployed in FY27; DFT mill + power plant INR200 cr (INR100 cr FY27, INR100 cr FY28); rooftop solar INR25 cr (INR10-12 cr FY27, INR13 cr FY28)
items.quote: Yes, so currently for the Kesda plant, which is currently the INR930 crores, so most of the money will be deployed in this year itself. And we have also announced power plant of INR200 crores along with the DFT mill, so that will have INR100 crores expenditure this year and INR100 crores expenditure next financial year.

items.statement: Brownfield stainless CR coil capacity doubled from 58,000 to 116,000 tpa at Kuthrel Unit 2; consent to operate received
items.quote: We are pleased to announce the successful completion of brownfield expansion of our stainless-steel CR coil facility at Kuthrel Unit 2. Our debottlenecking initiative has doubled our production capacity from 58,000 tons per annum to 1,16,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: Kesda greenfield + Kuthrel Unit 2 on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning; all orders placed, civil work on schedule
items.quote: Our Greenfield project at K esda and Kuthrel Unit 2 continue to progress well and remain on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27. We continue to make steady progress in our project execution, with a ll orders placed and civil work progressing on schedule

items.statement: Target total finished product capacity >2 million tpa by 2030 from current 0.68 million tpa
items.quote: We continue to make steady progress on our capacity expansion roadmap and remain on track to increase our total finished product capacity from 0.68 million tons per annum to over 2 million tons per annum by 2030.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton INR10,000 (excl. sponge iron); Q1 EBITDA margin 13%, PAT margin >7%
items.quote: This reflects our continued focus on superior product mix and higher margin value-added products and resulted in 19% year-on-year increase in EBITDA to INR10,000 per ton, excluding sponge iron sales.

items.quote: In terms of MS pipe, the pricing start to softening, if you looking at the other large players' commentary. So price is going to be stabilized, let's say, around, let's say, another 3% to 5% downward for this financial year we are looking at where the price will stabilize.

items.statement: Shifted from LPG to PNG (GAIL) in Jan 2026; uninterrupted supply, no cost/supply impact from war situation

items.statement: Secured product approvals from Engineers India Limited and Chennai Metro Rail Limited in Q1
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured product approvals from leading government organizations, including Engineers India Limited and Chennai Metro Rail Limited.

items.statement: Not directly competing with Jindal Stainless: JSL focuses >1mm thickness, >1200mm width; Sambhv focuses narrow width (330mm now, 650mm future) and ultra-thin 0.1-0.4mm (import substitution)

items.quote: And in this we have also qualified for PLI, in which we will get approximately 13% of our revenue from the central government as our incentive till 2030.

items.statement: Standalone fastener business remains net debt free and strongly cash generative; funds EV investments internally
items.quote: Importantly, our standalone fasteners business continues to remain strongly cash generative and net debt free, providing a solid financial foundation to internally support our long-term investments across EV and technology-led growth initiatives.

items.statement: Holdco investment in subsidiaries: ~INR50 cr in STML, ~INR48-49 cr in SEM (total ~INR100 cr); no external fund raise mentioned
items.quote: So we have invested -- our current investment in STML is INR50-odd crores and our current investment in SEM, also from a cash investment perspective is again about INR48 crores to INR49 crores. So maybe INR100 crores investment in both the businesses.

items.statement: SEM lost INR280 cr anchor customer revenue in FY25 (in-sourcing); ongoing R&D and validation spend drives losses; STML export opportunity 2-3 years out; EV ecosystem ramp-up slow
items.quote: In FY25, SEM business has clocked about INR380 crores of revenue backed on one large key anchor customer. That key anchor customer in-sourced their product. We lost close to INR280-odd crores of revenue in just 1 year.

items.statement: SEM team ~130 people, >50% in product/application engineering; heavy investment in engineering talent for localization and new product development
items.quote: Just to give you a perspective, we have about 130 people in our organization. More than half are in product or application engineering, okay? And that investment is crucial for the future.

items.statement: Targets 11-12% volume growth, ~3% net price hikes, 13-15% overall revenue growth, and 20-25% PAT growth for FY27
items.quote: Yeah, so we are very much clear about volume growth in the range of 11% to 12% volume growth and price hikes net of about around 3%. So overall like in the range of 13% to 15% on overall growth we will be go with that. And obviously then it will be my profit will be increase in the range of certainly 20% to 25% for the overall year at PAT level.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin improvement of 100-150 bps for FY27
items.quote: And with the obviously decent margin level which we targeted to be improve at least 100 basis points to 150 basis points in this overall year. So surely we going on that path.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 125-140 crores for FY27, with ~INR 20 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: So yes, so this year capex is around INR125 crores to INR140 crores. And for out of that we already did around INR20 crores expenditure in that because as we mentioned ongoing constructions at three -four sites.

items.statement: Two hubs automated (Tajnagar, Chakan); two more under construction (Kolkata by Mar/Jun'27, Ahmedabad by mid-FY28)
items.quote: So basically yes, so we already did two automation, and one again in Tajnagar, North India and Chakan, Pune. And two are in pipeline. So next would be Kolkata and Ahmedabad and they are right now in under construction.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 11.7% from 11.5% YoY; PAT margin 7.1%
items.quote: EBITDA grew 11% to INR 37 crores from last year, with margin expanding to 11.7% from 11.5% of last year. Profit after tax rose to 6% to INR 22.4 crores compared to INR 21 crores in Q1 of last year, with a margin of 7.1%.

items.statement: Fuel surcharge hike passed to 90%+ customers in June; combined with annual hikes, effective mid-single-digit price increase
items.quote: So we held the price hikes because we know about that government will be certainly increase the prices fuel after, elections. That's why we held up and so that's way we had taken the good price hike in June month in combined with obviously like annual price hikes also and diesel hike close also. So both put together is an handsome price hike we have taken.

items.statement: Healthy demand across manufacturing (pharma, engineering, electric, auto, SMEs); outsourced logistics shift benefits company
items.quote: Demand continued to be healthy across manufacturing, especially in pharmaceuticals, engineering, Electric, auto vehicles, and SME-led shipments, and the accelerating shift towards outsourced logistics players added directly to our strengths.

items.statement: Clear pipeline visibility for coming quarters; SME/B2B mix improved to 50:50 from 48:52
items.quote: So this time again in this quarter, SME is really bounced back. Earlier in last whole FY26, our mix was 48 -52, 48 SME and 52 B2B, means big customers. And now in this quarter, start with the very good note as a 50-50, which we desire for that actually.

items.statement: E-commerce Express surged 63% YoY (now 2-2.5% of revenue); Domestic Air +29%, International +27%, Surface +9%, C2C strong
items.quote: The star of the quarter was our E-commerce Express business, which surged 63% year-on-year to become our fastest -growing service vertical by a wide margin, driven by rising volumes from E -commerce platforms and direct-to-consumer brands.

items.statement: Receivables 58 days, payables 32 days, net working cycle 26-27 days; improved cash conversion
items.quote: Receivables stood at around 58 days, payables improved to like 32 days, and net working cycle therefore it is 26 -27 days. A strong sign of better cash conversion in the company.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 118 crores as of June 30, 2026; remains debt-free
items.quote: Our balance sheet is in great shape with net cash of around INR 118 crores as on June 30th, 2026.

items.statement: Volume growth of 7.5% YoY to 250,000 metric tonnes in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Volume number for this quarter is 2,50,000 metric ton in Q1. It is a growth of around in volume-wise, this is a growth of around 7.5% in this tonnage numbers.

items.statement: E-commerce strategy targets small merchants/D2C (16-18% EBITDA), not large platforms; expanding regional teams, branches, biker fleet
items.quote: We are going on the small customers, which is allow us to be getting the margin. So this is very clear strategy actually from day one. And again, it's not like we are doing crores of business in that, it is a very small business and we will be thoughtfully with the margin we will be only going with that.

items.statement: Management expects 20-25% revenue growth for FY27, not formal guidance but ambition
items.quote: we do believe that probably for the whole year, we could be achieving about at least between a 20% to 25% growth in this financial year

items.statement: Medium-term target of 10% PBT margin in next 3-4 years
items.quote: Our long-term strategy is to take it to 10% PBT in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Overseas electronics and lighting revenue expected to double in FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: we believe that this year, the -- our revenue in the overseas business can and I'm sure I'm referring to the overseas electronics and lighting business. This can be double.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR500-550 crores for FY27 including India and overseas
items.quote: It will be INR500 crores to INR550 crores in that range. This includes both India and overseas.

items.statement: Strong automotive demand in Q1 FY27 with 2-wheelers up 22.8%, 3-wheelers 39.1%, PVs 16.8%, CVs 15.2% YoY
items.quote: On a year -on-year basis, 2 -wheelers grew by 22.8%, 3 -wheelers grew by 39.1%, passenger vehicles grew by 16.8% and commercial vehicles grew by 15.2%.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler volumes grew 91% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The EV 2- wheeler volume on a year-on-year basis grew by 91%.

items.statement: India operations EBITDA margin 10.6% and PBT margin ~7% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Despite that, the Indian operations reported a 10.6% EBITDA margin and around a 7% PBT margin.

items.statement: War-related under-recovery of 50 bps expected to recover mostly between Q2 and Q3 FY27
items.quote: So we should be getting it between this quarter and next quarter, most of it.

items.statement: Net new business wins of INR5,991 million annualized peak revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: In quarter 1 of financial year '27, our net new business wins with an annualized peak revenues of INR5,991 million.

items.statement: Order book started at INR3,509 crores, added ~INR600 crores in Q1, ~INR500 crores moved to SOP
items.quote: So we started with INR3,509 crores at the beginning of the year. Current quarter, we added close to INR600 crores. Out of that, close to INR500 crores has been taken to start of production already.

items.statement: Traction motor SOP starting Q2 FY27 with one customer, two more expected in FY27
items.quote: we've already announced one business win, which we will SOP begin immediately, I would imagine, in fact, in quarter 2. And then there is 2 further customers where I would say we are in fairly advanced discussion, where also I would expect SOPs to take place in this financial year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex ~INR160 crores, mostly for capacity increases; front-loaded for the year
items.quote: capex during quarter 1 was about INR160 crores. Most of it went into the capacity increases.

items.statement: Significant capex increase in FY27 vs last 2-3 years, largely for e-mobility capacity expansion
items.quote: this year, we will definitely see higher capex expenditure than what we've seen over the last 2, 3 years. And a large portion of that is, yes, in terms of our e-mobility capacity expansion

items.statement: Overseas losses reducing sequentially; Romania electronics targeting EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27
items.quote: In Romania, we will reach EBITDA breakeven.

items.statement: EV revenue 15.8% of total in Q1 FY27, up 87% YoY; ~75% from Bajaj Auto
items.quote: The revenue from supplying to electric vehicles in this quarter was around 15.8% of revenue and grew by 87% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Company ~70% powertrain agnostic, balance from ICE and e-powertrain; EV share of growth increasing
items.quote: In fact, I would say where we're I think only around 70% powertrain agnostic. The balance comes from our ICE powertrain, e-powertrain business.

items.statement: Engaged with all top 3 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler EV players; won non-powertrain business from one, e-powertrain discussions with another
items.quote: With one of them, we are in discussion for the e-powertrain. With another one of them, we've already won business for another technology product, which we have declared in Q1.

items.statement: Direct business with KTM pre-takeover; incremental opportunities post-Bajaj acquisition
items.quote: we already do -- even prior to this, we did a fair amount of direct business with KTM. And post this, I would say, more complete takeover, there is incremental opportunities that arise

items.statement: Strategy is product-line and competence-driven, not customer diversification; Bajaj remains key but other customers growing
items.quote: our path forward is really a product line -- a product line and competence-driven strategy. So there is clear product lines where we look to d rive growth and where we look to drive focus

items.statement: Net working capital increased INR441 million in Q1 due to higher revenues and war-related recoveries pending invoicing
items.quote: mainly due to the increase in net working capital of INR441 million due to higher revenues.

items.statement: No change in receivable days; inventory up for peak season preparation and war-related recoveries
items.quote: there is no change receivable days. Yes, inventory went up to some extent, largely in preparation to the peak season, which is coming up. Second thing is the war -related recoveries

items.statement: Net debt INR5,268 million (INR527 crores) in Q1 FY27, up INR316 million QoQ; net debt/equity 0.28, net debt/EBITDA <0.6
items.quote: The net debt of the company in quarter 1 of FY financial year '27 is INR5,268 million, which is an increase of INR316 million from the last quarter

items.statement: Zero debt target maintained for FY28 despite Q1 increase
items.quote: We'll stay with that for now. But yes, we will always try to do it as soon as possible.

items.statement: Appointed Eric Hammond as CTO for Business Unit 1 with 25 years global automotive tech experience
items.quote: Recently, we have appointed Mr. Eric Hammond as a Chief Technology Officer for our Business Unit 1. He comes in with 25 years of global automotive technology and engineering leadership experience

items.statement: Open to inorganic opportunities in electronics, e-powertrain, aftermarket (4-wheeler/exports), primarily in India
items.quote: we would be more keen on either it could be electronics or e -powertrain, these areas and also in the area of aftermarket. Aftermarket also, we are experiencing a strong growth. So -- and I would say more on the 4-wheeler or the exports front.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 24.6% in Q1 FY27 from 23.6% YoY; ROE improved to 16.4% from 11%; annualized EPS INR20.3 vs INR11.5
items.quote: If you compare the ROCE last year, same time, we were at 23.6%. It went up to 24.6% now. A significant improvement in return on equity also from 11% to 16.4% this time. And in terms of EPS also, last time, it was INR11.5 on an annualized basis, which is now INR20.3 on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Ongoing commodity price volatility and geopolitical uncertainties (Iran war) cited as risks
items.quote: Despite the ongoing risk from commodity price volatility and global geopolitical uncertainties, the overall outlook for financial year '27 remains positive

items.statement: Management reaffirmed full-year PAT growth guidance of 40-50% and expects Q3/Q4 to show a big leap after Q1/Q2 investment phase
items.quote: So we are fully committed to achieve our guidance number and we are focused on achieving those

items.statement: Q1 gross profit grew 15% YoY but PAT and EBITDA margins dipped due to growth investments in manpower and technology across direct and indirect costs
items.quote: There's been a strong growth in gross profit of 15% Q1 '27 over Q1 '26. However, the investment made around manpower and technology has impacted PAT and EBITDA ma rgin in the immediate term

items.statement: Adjusted for growth investments, PBT would have been higher by INR 4 crores and gross profit by INR 2.5 crores in Q1
items.quote: Would like to bring your attention, adjusted for these growth and investment, we would have grown our PBT by almost INR 4 crores and our gross profit by almost INR 2.5 crore, which is a pretty healthy growth.

items.statement: Insurance revenue reached INR 15 crores in Q1 vs INR 24 crores in Q4; delinquent loan collection also grew substantially despite seasonally slow quarter
items.quote: Just to tell you, insurance las t quarter was INR 24 crores in terms of revenue, which we have done clocked a revenue of INR 15 crores in this this quarter itself

items.statement: BC network acquisition down only 10% vs industry decline of 8% in Q1; multi-product Sahayaks (3-4 products) increased showing stickiness
items.quote: despite the in dustry being slow in during the first quarter by 8%, it did not matter. We were down by only 10% on th e BC network acquisition

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution to launch by fag end of Q2 or early Q3, initially through Sahayak network
items.quote: we will be very soon getting into mutual fund distribution. We will largely focus on Sahayaks in the first scope, and hopefully that product should go live in the fa g end of quarter two or early quarter

items.statement: Asset distribution via CRA arrangement with large private bank to start by fag end of Q2 or early Q3
items.quote: We recently got into a tie-up with a very large private sector bank for the CRA arrangement. We started, as I said, we will be starting asset distribution by the fag end of quarter two or early quarter one.

items.statement: UPI cash withdrawal product maturing with PhonePe entry; PaySprint payment orchestration platform AI-driven and scaling
items.quote: UPI cash withdrawal pro duct has recently been added and now becoming mature by phone PhonePe coming in to the picture. So, and also our payment orchestration platform, which is highly AI trained and AI driven

items.statement: Remittance business (AD-II license) and asset BC lending targeted for Phase 2 later in the year
items.quote: For an exchange, following the AD- II license, the remittance business will come into the picture. There are few guidelines which are there which will help us increase our remittance business, also the asset BC lending.

items.statement: Regulatory changes wiped out L0 and face authentication in AePS; new OTP requirement for withdrawals above INR 5,000 creating near-term headwinds
items.quote: Today if the customer wants to withdraw more than INR 5000 in one go, there is a OTP which goes on the registered mobile number of the customer linked with

items.statement: RBI queries on Payworld PPI license change of control in final phase; outcome expected soon to enable money and PPI products at scale
items.quote: Payworld, on the smart payment license which was on the cha nge of control, we are in the last phase of the queries from the RBI. So we might see the outcome v ery soon

items.statement: Significant Q1 investment in hiring experienced leadership, on-ground distribution manpower, insurance telemarketing and POS teams; continuing in Q2
items.quote: The on-ground employees which we have hired for various services, d elinquency or maybe distribution business for adding more Sahayaks or on the insuranc e side we have added telemarketing setups, those or insurance POS also manpower for insurance POS

items.statement: Building regional L&D structure for vernacular training of Sahayaks to cross-sell multiple financial products
items.quote: Also the setup just to add in building a L&D team structure at a regional le vel. We understand the core products will continue to face regulatory headwinds and to re ally insulate ourselves from these headwinds, we want to be better prepared for

items.statement: Active Sahayak count declined due to regulatory changes but multi-product adoption (3-4 products) increased, indicating stickiness
items.quote: the multi-product adoption in our Sahayak network is in creased over the year, but single product has gone down due to consolidation of network by part-time Sahayaks who have either by the regulatory change actually where L0 (L Zero) has been wiped out and face authentication also has been wiped out

items.statement: ARPU expected to normalize from current level to INR 1,200-1,500 range as regulatory clarity enables consolidation
items.quote: the average which we see is about, it will go from 1,200 to 1,500 ARP U. The ARPU should be increasing

items.statement: No single Sahayak contributes more than 0.1% of revenue; network depth enables cross-sell and product expansion
items.quote: the higher granular revenue base with no Sahayak contributing to more than 0.1% of our revenue. The strong n etwork depth provides a platform for cross-sell, deeper engagement, and future product expansion

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Yatra.com signed; expanding Sahayak and distributor capabilities to sell multiple banking and financial products
items.quote: We recently got an opportunity to get into a strategic partnership with Yatra.co m, plus as I said, we are really focusing around building capabilities with our Sahayak s, our own sales teams on ground, and distributors to be able to sell multiple products across the spectrum of banking and financial services

items.statement: Forex revenue up ~5% but segment PBT fell from INR 27.14 to -17.57 due to margin compression from competition despite higher dollar prices
items.quote: Forex because of the global e conomic conditions, the volume was there because of the prices of dollars and everything going high, the volume that's why the revenue jump is been able to see. But in the margin-wise, the margi ns were not there due to competition in the market

items.statement: Payworld travel network scaling well and supporting forex/remittance growth; Payworld currently at break-even
items.quote: the Payworld side also, the travel network what Payworld has been there for us has been doing very fantastic for us and we are scaling on the travel network there, which will help us to scale our forex and remittance business as well, which goes hand- in-hand along with the travel network there. So Payworld again is break-even for us right

items.statement: Sameer Nagpal joined as Group COO in first week of July to lead distribution and cross-sell execution
items.quote: Apart from that, we are investing in more leadership people in Q2 like Same er has joined us in July first week. So that is the big change which we have brought

items.statement: AePS product maturity means recurring regulatory changes (e.g., new OTP rule for >INR 5,000 withdrawals) will continue to create near-term turbulence
items.quote: this AePS product has reached a certain level of maturity. The product is mature a nd therefore we will continue to see regulatory changes hitting this product every now

items.statement: AI being used across product development, sales automation (paperless goal), fraud prevention (FRM tools), and vernacular training modules for Sahayaks
items.quote: we are using AI to the fullest to turn ar ound products in the shortest span of time. In-house, we're building a sales automation tool. The d ream is to make sales organization a paperless organization

items.statement: Credit growth guidance for FY27 is 14-15%
items.quote: We believe that maybe the nominal GDP would be around 12% to 12.5% and SBI has always grown 2% to 3% more than that. That is the reason I have given the credit growth guidance of 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Domestic NIM guidance for FY27 maintained at 3%
items.quote: Margin outlook, I still hold, I am not going to give you quarterly outlook. This is a full year outlook of 3%, which I mentioned right in the beginning of my speech. We are sticking to that.

items.statement: Domestic NIM remained resilient at 3% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our domestic Net Interest Margin remained resilient at 3%, reinforcing our confidence in maintaining our guidance for the financial year.

items.statement: Cost of deposits decreased by ~7 bps in Q1 FY27
items.quote: An almost 7 basis point uptick has come mainly because of the cost of deposits going down.

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline exceeds ₹9 lakh crore including undisbursed term loans, unutilized working capital and pipeline
items.quote: Overall, if you include the undisbursed term loans, unutilized working capital and pipeline, it exceeds ₹9 lakh crore.

items.statement: Total business crossed ₹110 trillion, deposits exceeded ₹60 trillion, advances crossed ₹50 trillion
items.quote: Our balance sheet continued to expand with the total business crossing ₹110 trillion, while deposits exceeded the ₹60 trillion mark and advances crossed the ₹50 trillion mark.

items.statement: Retail term deposit growth at 14%, savings bank deposits grew 10% to ₹17.5 lakh crore
items.quote: If you see our retail deposit, term deposit growth is 14%, continues to be 14%. And more notably, savings bank with a balance of ₹17.5 lakh crore base has grown by 10%.

items.statement: Excess SLR of ₹3.06 lakh crore as of June 30, ₹4 lakh crore currently with FCNR(B) flows
items.quote: on 30 th June, we had an excess SLR of ₹3.06 lakh crore. And as we speak, also contributed by the FCNR (B) flows, we have State Bank of India August 07, 2026 6 excess SLR of ₹4 lakh crore

items.statement: Mobilized $6 billion FCNR(B) deposits, $1 billion OFCB, $300 million ECBs totaling ~$7.3 billion
items.quote: We have had almost $6 billion FCNR (B) deposit mobilized. And we also have done OFCB of $1 billion, and $300 million of ECBs. So, in all about $7.3 billion have been funded by mostly our foreign offices.

items.statement: Expect total FCNR(B) mobilization of ~$10 billion (₹1 lakh crore) for FY27
items.quote: If we have ₹1 lakh crore flows of FCNR(B) which we expect to have, I think to that extent predominantly it will be reducing our bulk proportion.

items.statement: Fresh slippages ₹7,046 crore in Q1 FY27, ₹1,400 crore already pulled back
items.quote: During Q1 FY27 our fresh slippages were ₹7,046 crore, out of which we have already pulled back ₹1,400 crore as on date.

items.statement: Gross and net NPA ratios at lowest level in over two decades
items.quote: Gross and net NPA ratios have further improved and remained at their lowest level in over two decades.

items.statement: Segmental fresh slippages: Agri ₹2,600 crore, SME ₹2,300 crore, Personal ₹2,100 crore
items.quote: And segmental numbers are also given, but I will just read out. Agri- ₹2,600 Cr, SME- ₹2,300 crore, personal segment- ₹2,100 Cr.

items.statement: Corporate loan pricing transitioning from T-bill linked to MCLR, work in progress
items.quote: So, what we see on the corporate side is a combination of moving a part of that portfolio to MCLR and obviously in the process somebody who is not willing to pay MCLR have looked for alternatives.

items.statement: Gold loan book crossed ₹3.1 trillion (personal ₹1.25 trillion, agri ₹1.85 trillion) as of June 30
items.quote: So, our personal gold loans is of the order of ₹1.25 trillion and Agri gold loans is of the order of ₹1.85 trillion. So, both put together, we crossed ₹3.1 trillion as of 30 th June

items.statement: Xpress Credit growth limited as customers opt for gold loans due to 3% rate arbitrage
items.quote: But it is not going into double-digit territory because of the gold loans. We have seen that many of the normal Xpress Credit customers are opting to take gold loan. Obviously, there is an interest rate arbitrage, almost 3%.

items.statement: Building collection vertical with 6,000 Feet on Street via SBOSS subsidiary to deepen self-employed lending
items.quote: We are creating Feet on Street across the country. Almost 6,000 is our estimated number, which we will be deploying as Feet on Street through SBOSS, our subsidiary.

items.statement: ECL implementation assessment delayed; models to be pushed to IT systems by August 18; numbers expected in Q2
items.quote: My team tells me that 18th August, probably they would be pushing all the models and data into the IT system. The correct way of doing it is that probably when we meet again in Q2, we will give you the numbers.

items.statement: ECL impact not expected to be major; will use regulatory transition dispensation and capital from MF listing
items.quote: But one assurance I can give you, it will not have any major impact for two reasons. One is that we will have some capital augmentation because of the mutual fund and hopefully on the other major divestment which we are planning.

items.statement: Miscellaneous expenses: insurance expenses ₹1,723 crore vs ₹2,074 crore YoY; other misc expenses ₹2,385 crore vs ₹2,266 crore YoY
items.quote: And the insurance expenses as against ₹2,074 crore in Q1 last year, we have incurred ₹1,723 crore.

items.statement: PLI provisions of ~₹3,000 crore spread over four quarters (₹750-800 crore per quarter) instead of Q4 lump sum
items.quote: See, the PLI provision may be back-ended last year but we decided to spread out four quarters this year.

items.statement: Interest on income tax refund ₹220 crore in Q1 FY27 vs ₹1,002 crore in Q4 FY26
items.quote: ₹220 crore is what we have, interest on IT.

items.statement: Forex fee income bottomed out at ₹500 crore in Q1 due to NOP guidelines and war volatility; expected to improve
items.quote: We believe that the forex fee income has bottomed out in 1Q and we should be able to deliver better in the forthcoming quarters.

items.statement: SBI General Insurance is next candidate for listing but no timeline given
items.quote: I am still sticking that SBI General is the next candida te for listing but no timeline

items.statement: CASA franchise remains one of strongest in industry; non-government current account deposits grew 14%
items.quote: 14% growth in non-governmental deposits. This is what is actually very inte resting to note, that while we have been one of the biggest current account holders for the government balances. That is drying up. Still, we are holding on the current account market share because our penetration in the non -governmental is increasing significantly

items.statement: CHAKRA Centre of Excellence building capability for emerging sectors (data centers, hydrogen, solar, M&A)
items.quote: This is what Mr. Tewari has mentioned in terms of our Centre of Excellence, CHAKRA initiative so that at least a dedicated team of people who understand the emerging industries , n ot only opportunities , and the risk associated with funding them

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR875-910 crores
items.quote: We continue to target Financial Year '27 revenue in the range of INR875 crores to INR910 crores, while maintaining healthy profitability, and remain committed to our long-term objective of building a INR2,000 crores to INR2,200 crores revenue platform with a INR200-plus crores PAT by Financial Year '30.

items.statement: Current order book INR1,312.53 crores
items.quote: Our current order book number is INR 1,312.53 crores.

items.statement: EPC order book >INR800 crores, combined with BESS >INR1,300 crores
items.quote: So at present, our current order booking is more than INR800 crores in just EPC, and combining with BESS, it's more than INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: Bids under evaluation >INR1,400 crores, active bidding >INR2,600 crores
items.quote: The bidding under evaluation is more than INR1,400 crores, and the projects which we are bidding are more than INR2,600 crores.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book plus L1 positions ~INR840 crores
items.quote: So at present, the unexecuted order booking plus in which we are L1 is around INR840 crores.

items.statement: Expecting LOA of ~INR100 crores from DGVCL where L1
items.quote: So in DGVCL, we are expecting the LOA of around INR100 crores of single tender in which we were L1.

items.statement: Greenfield transformer project Phase 1 capex ~INR90 crores, spent INR3.5-4 crores so far, FY27 capex ~INR10 crores
items.quote: So total capex for the greenfield project for the first phase would be around INR90 crores. Out of that, we have spent around INR3.5- INR4 crores so far. items.statement: Transformer facility Phase 1: 20 MVA capacity by end FY27, 132 kV/63 MVA by FY28, scaling to 200 kV/400 kV

items.statement: Inaugurating 10 MVA transformer facility (eligible up to 20 MVA) by end of current month

items.quote: currently it is uh less than 1,000 rupees and uh I think it should go down much below that as we

items.quote: We hope that uh we grow as much as we have grown year on year in the first quarter. We would like to see similar results in the second quarter as well.

items.statement: No acquisition plans currently; focus on core organic growth; cash to be used as working capital
items.quote: As of now we are not looking to buy out. Mithun Maity: organically Dr Vikas Aggarwal: We have understood that uh we have to focus on our core

items.quote: I think 100% % sales is happening in India. Maybe there might be some orders coming from outside India. Uh maybe like some numbers like 10 15 maximum.

items.quote: We are still not sure that uh we should go beyond 33% gross margins in future. We want to pass the benefit to our customers in long term.

items.statement: Marketing spend held tight this quarter — helped cost base but hurts top-of-funnel; balancing spend vs recovered margins not yet perfected
items.quote: We held marketing spend very tight this quarter. That was the right call for the cost base and you can see the benefits in the results but it has a cost of its own at the top of the funnel and we can see that cost.

items.quote: membership customers have a uh a slightly lower average order value but uh double the rule so if we if we can sell more membership in future. It is beneficial for both the customers as well as the company.

items.statement: International brands (e.g., Septodont) grow faster on Dentalkart; platform neutrality and reach to underserved towns valued by MNCs
items.quote: we were doing for example 100 rupees with them. Now we are doing 250 rupees with them. Dr Vikas Aggarwal: And the overall sales in India uh is also growing

items.statement: Export compliances exist for many products but not pursuing exports; focus on domestic opportunity
items.quote: there are compliances involved in our industry for exports and uh however we have uh many products which are uh you know having that compliance but we're not looking at exports right now

items.statement: Warranty/returns/refunds: 80-90% resolved within TAT; edge cases remain; automating SOPs via AI to improve consistency
items.quote: 80 to 90% of the warranty claims, returns and refunds happen within the tag. Dr Vikas Aggarwal: It is the uh edge cases where we lack and we have to minimize the edge cases going forward

items.statement: Management expects Q2 FY27 top line slightly better than Q1 and similar profitability momentum; full-year FY27 revenue not significantly higher than FY26 as focus is on margin building over top-line growth
items.quote: The pipelines, the CRM and the pipelines tell me that Q2 top lines could be slightly better than Q1 itself.

items.statement: Management expects current EBITDA margins sustainable for FY27 and possibly FY28 due to hardware price volatility and execution
items.quote: for the current ﬁnancial year, we feel that these margins are pretty much sustainable and the coming quarters will also reﬂect similar sentiments

items.statement: Management attributes margin improvement to execution, strategy, and hardware price volatility; expects similar momentum in Q2
items.quote: the current margins reﬂect not only proper execution and right strategy which went into place but also it reﬂects the current market conditions. The hardware price volatility has played some role in building up these margins

items.statement: Structural growth drivers identified: AI infrastructure, data sovereignty, cybersecurity, cloud adoption, digital transformation; pipelines strong for Q2 and long-term
items.quote: Key structural growth drivers include: Artiﬁcial Intelligence Infrastructure: Increasing adoption of AI is accelerating demand for GPU computing and advanced infrastructure. Data Sovereignty: Government regulations and enterprise requirements are driving demand for secure domestic

items.statement: No traditional order book model; execution cycle 60-90 days; estimated order book ~₹20-25 crore as of 30 June 2026; hardware pipeline ~₹100 crore but not imminent
items.quote: So, on 30th June, if I do a guesstimate, our order book might be standing at somewhere close to around 20-25 crores, not more than that.

items.statement: No SMT line investment planned; will use third-party job work for PCB assembly; Zeacloud asset-heavy with depreciation impact
items.quote: There is no need for me to establish an SMT line ever. What does an SMT line do? SMT line is a tool to populate your PCB and there is so much of spare capacity available in India itself on SMT lines.

items.statement: HexaData HPC orchestration platform v1 ready and shipping; Zeacloud stack complete except observability module; MeitY empanelment process underway targeting completion this FY
items.quote: Exadata HPC platform version 1 is ready, ready to ship to customers. We have already been doing POCs and demonstrating it to our customers, to relevant customers and hope to ship it out commercially very soon.

items.statement: No fundraising plans for current financial year FY27
items.quote: in the current ﬁnancial year, there are no plans to raise any funds. That's a clear no from us till now

items.statement: MeitY empanelment for Zeacloud: internal certifications (ISO) targeted by September 2026, then 3-4 month MeitY process; expected within FY27

items.statement: Government revenue ~40-45% of FY26; lower in current year but targeting higher-value government bids; not dependent on government; already compete with Cisco, HP, Lenovo, Dell

items.quote: We are competing already with foreign vendors, be it Cisco, be it HP, be it Lenovo, be it Dell. We partner with them also; we do sell their products and brands as well as we compete with them also in certain deals.

items.statement: R&D spend <2% of revenue (mostly HexaData); Zeacloud R&D higher % but small revenue base; currently expensed, may capitalize under Ind AS in 2-3 years
items.quote: Looking at the total revenues, it might hardly be less than 2% of the total revenue, which goes towards R&D as of now in Esconet.

items.statement: Force majeure events (wars, supply chain disruptions) could impact Q3/Q4; hardware price volatility benefit may not persist beyond FY28
items.quote: We have seen out of the blue wars happening and supply chains getting disrupted and nobody has a control. So, that kind of force majeure situation may disrupt anything which nobody may have control over it.

items.statement: Voluntary quarterly reporting initiated from Q1 FY27; will continue Q1-Q4 cadence; first quarterly disclosure for NSE SME-listed company
items.quote: Q1 FY2026-27 is Esconet Technologies Limited's ﬁrst-ever voluntary quarterly ﬁnancial disclosure. While NSE SME-listed companies are generally required to report their ﬁnancial performance on a half-yearly basis, management has taken a conscious decision to move beyond the minimum reporting requirement

items.statement: Maintain FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20% and profitability growth faster than revenue
items.quote: Correct. So, as far as the financial year targets are concerned, yes, we will maintain the same guidance.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately INR350 crores as of today
items.quote: But as of today, we have an order book of about INR350 crores. That's what I can say.

items.quote: Back-to-back what we have done is we have placed orders for four high-speed FRP pilot and security boats with an option of two additional boats.

items.statement: Fleet expansion to strengthen pilotage and security services capabilities; four new FRP boats ordered with option for two more
items.quote: These vessels will strengthen our capabilities in the pilotage and security services that we provide and it will add our capacities for the future as well.

items.statement: Monsoon season impacts some asset deployment but contracts outside weather window and foreign water deployment of Saroja Blessing offset revenue loss
items.quote: However, we have managed to tide over this and take contracts outside the outside the weather window and also performed that as well.

items.statement: Port services offer best ROC with low capital cost and high EBITDA; offshore logistics margins lower
items.quote: So, I see a best ROC in the port services like just to give you a short answer, where the even though the capital cost is low, the return or rather the EBITDA is pretty high, I would say.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue mix: INR25.4 crores offshore logistics, INR3.13 crores oil spill response, INR2.68 crores port services
items.quote: So, we have done INR25 crores -- INR25.4 crores in offshore logistics, INR3.13 crores in oil spill response and INR2.68 crores in port services. Total INR31.21 crores.

items.quote: A significant development during the quarter was the award of a seven-year pilot launch services from Mumbai Port, valued at approximately INR18 crores.

items.quote: Our fleet utilization across the port services about 95% and across the offshore logistics side is about 80% to 85%.

items.quote: At present, we are having about INR10 crores. Accordingly, the size of the turnover we will require accordingly 20% to 25%.

items.period: early next year or mid-next year

items.quote: In general I would say like for India market, I would say they are softening, but with caution, they will also come up in some time.

items.statement: Key bottlenecks: time for tenders to materialize and availability of quality second-hand offshore vessels at reasonable prices
items.quote: Number one, the time taken for tenders to materialize. Number two, the availability of quality assets at the price that we are looking at because unless it makes business sense, we will not go into those assets at all.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR250 crores across all businesses, with INR75 crores from geotech and water combined and the balance from parks
items.quote: The total revenue, which we are looking at across all our businesses is around INR250-odd crores and which includes around INR75 crores or so from the geotech and the water business together and the balance probably from the Park side of the business.

items.quote: We are reasonably sure to probably open anywhere close to 25 to 30 operating parks by end of March.

items.quote: As of now, the inquiry funnel across our -- all our businesses remains close to around INR1,500-plus crores, which includes parks, which includes geotech, which includes the water part of the business.

items.statement: Recurring revenue from park operations targeted at INR40 crores in FY27, up 5x from INR8 crores in FY26
items.quote: Our current year numbers from the operation is around target for this year is around INR40 crores. This is in comparison to INR8 crores in last year, so which is almost five times growth.

items.quote: So if I look at overall my total Park revenue of around INR130-odd crores construction and around INR40 crores out of this thing INR170 crores, probably we are talking about 25%-odd as a revenue from the recurring operations this year. Next year, it can go high to almost 40%. I think in three years, probably it should stabilize at that around 60% of our revenue comes from the recurring side

items.statement: Park execution timeline of 6 months (180 days) guaranteed once land is available, with one park built in 4 months for PM inauguration
items.quote: We definitely can execute any project provided land is clearly available to us in a six months period. You know, the pitch which we have given recently into various Head of States is that, you give us any park we guarantee delivery within 180 days.

items.quote: In the other Lucknow parks, our investments were in the range of around 26%-odd. In this case, we chose to go a little higher, seeing the strategic advantage of the location and the terms and conditions of the contracts which we could negotiate.

items.statement: Debtors over 180 days reduced to 15% of total debtors, showing improvement but not yet at desirable levels
items.quote: Our total 180 days and above debtors are only what, 15%, of the overall debtors. So we are improving and we continue to have very strong focus on that.

items.statement: Currently 9 fully operational parks, 4 ready for inauguration, 7 under construction, 3 at award stage, and 11 in tendering stage
