items.quote: Just last week, we started our first park in Jammu and Kashmir at Jammu called Tawi Wonderland with a very thunderous market response and which proves our strategy that there is a need for such parks across the country.

items.statement: Integrating geosynthetics and water recycling capabilities into park projects (e.g., Patna park landfilling, embedded recycling plants) creating unique competitive positioning
items.quote: This combination of geosynthetics and water blending into Park also gives us a very unique positioning into that segment. And while we continue to pursue the importance of developing these parks, we also believe the importance of geosynthetics and the water recycling remains very high.

items.statement: Park inauguration timing dependent on government/VIP availability causing delays; 4 parks ready but awaiting inauguration; soft launch resisted by government partners
items.quote: We are not seeing any delay in the execution. We'll see delay in terms of the inauguration and which is something which I feel is beyond our control. Just an example, probably last week, Jammu Park got inaugurated by Honorable CM, Omar Abdullah-ji, but the park has been lying ready for almost several months.

items.statement: Building bench strength for recurring operations (marketing, events, F&B, kids activities) ahead of park openings, increasing salary costs in near term
items.quote: So if you would have noticed even in the current year numbers, the increase in the salary component, because we are continuously adding our strength in terms of doing the marketing events, activations, F&B, kids activities, and I think that's a part of the process before we start hitting the recurring margins in excess of 35%, 40%.

items.statement: Expect business to become self-funding by FY27-28 once recurring revenue reaches 35-40%, reducing need for external debt or equity
items.quote: I think by FY27-'28, I think once we reach a recurring revenue of almost 35%, 40%, we shouldn't be in a sufficient cash-generating situation.

items.statement: Backed out of water technology acquisition due to effectiveness concerns; no active acquisition targets currently
items.quote: As I mentioned in my previous call, probably because the technology didn't seem to be probably effective, we decided to back out of that acquisition. We continuously evaluate, but there is nothing which I would say is right now on the horizon.

items.statement: Strong demand for geosynthetics driven by landslides in hilly terrain and flood embankment needs during monsoon season
items.quote: The amount of land slides, which we see in the hilly terrains provides a significant opportunity in terms of what needs to be done using geosynthetics as a medium. Similarly, with the rains, with the floods, which comes in, in several parts of India, keeps giving us the opportunity of how do we ensure the flood embankments and those kind of things which gets built.

items.statement: Water scarcity and uneven rainfall driving wastewater management demand for Aqua vertical
items.quote: As the concerns about water scarcity revived by uneven rainfall across the country, and the effect have been driven businesses to double down on wastewater management.

items.statement: 60% of parks use differential weekday/weekend ticket pricing for crowd control; rest use flat rates; continuously evaluating pricing strategy
items.quote: Majority of our parks have -- I would say not majority, 60% of our parks have ticket of lesser on weekdays and higher on the weekends to probably better control the crowd. In some parks, we have a flat rate across all days of the week. And so that's something which we continuously evolve -- continuously evaluate to see what makes the maximum sense

items.statement: Park contracts typically 20-year terms (some 5+5 or 10+10); government cannot terminate without event of default; revenue share or fixed rental varies by park
items.quote: So majority of our parks are for 20 years, and these are contractual documents. Government can't change unless and until we probably do something terribly wrong there, and if there is an event of default, which I don't see any of such things probably in our case. And so we continue to have the period of 20 years.

items.statement: Creative Park division revenue INR22 crores in Q1 FY27 (+40% QoQ vs Q4 FY26), contributing ~75% of total revenue
items.quote: The FY26-'27, the Q1, the Creative Park division gave a result of almost INR22-odd crores compared to around INR15 crores in the previous quarter of '25-'26, representing a growth of over 40%. It contributed nearly 3/4 of our revenue from operations during the quarter

items.statement: Terra (geosynthetics) revenue INR7.5 crores in Q1 FY27 (+48% YoY from INR5 crores)
items.quote: The Terra vertical, which is the geosynthetic vertical, the revenue increased from almost INR5 crores to INR7.5 crores in this quarter of this year, a growth of approximately almost 48%.

items.statement: Geotech business targeting doubling of order book and revenue in FY27
items.quote: We are more than confident to probably reach our numbers in geotech business itself, we are doubling this year in terms of the order book and everything else which we have.

items.value: INR 10 billion intake; INR 45.9 billion backlog

Of the total order intake, 62% came from bioenergy, 28% from engineering, and the balance 10% from Praj HiPurity Systems business. The order backlog as of June 30, 2026, is at INR 45.9 billion, comprising 63% of domestic orders.

items.statement: Praj GenX targets EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27 driven by data center order execution
items.quote: So hopefully by end of this year, we should be able to see that break-even because our volume for the order book for Praj GenX is looking better now.

items.statement: Bio-isobutanol demo plant construction to complete by December 2026
items.quote: construction will get done and completed by end of this year, by December of 2026

items.statement: Domestic first-gen ethanol greenfield projects slow; inquiries only from ethanol deficit states like Tamil Nadu and Assam; strong demand for brownfield solutions and greenfield ENA plants
items.quote: Our first-generation ethanol domestic business continued to experience a slowdown in greenfield projects. Currently, inquiries for greenfield projects are only from customers in ethanol deficit areas of states like Tamil Nadu and Assam.

items.statement: International engagement in Brazil, USA (E15), Indonesia, Vietnam, Kenya, Panama, Argentina, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Bolivia driven by energy security and cost
items.quote: We are closely following the developments in the U.S.A. market also. U.S.A. has announced usage of E15, that is 15% blending in gasoline or petrol. We are also engaging with potential customers in Indonesia, Vietnam, Kenya, Panama, Argentina, Guatemala, Costa Rica, and Bolivia, where the governments are increasing the share of biofuels in their energy mix.

items.statement: GOBARdhan scheme approved with INR 23,000 crore outlay for FY27-FY36 to scale CBG production nearly tenfold with assured demand, pricing, capital assistance, pipeline infrastructure, credit support
items.quote: To establish Compressed Bio-Gas or CBG as a major pillar of India's future energy mix, the union cabinet has approved GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, with a total outlay of over INR 23,000 crores. Set for implementation between FY 2026-2027 to FY 2035-2036.

items.statement: Praj GenX secured USD 50 million global supply agreement over 2.5 years for modular hyperscale data center infrastructure, marking diversification beyond bioenergy

items.statement: Received order for detailed engineering of ethanol-to-SAF plant from international customer; ICAO approved sugarcane-to-jet pathway
items.quote: On the SAF front, we have received an order to deliver detailed engineering for ethanol-to-SAF plant from an international customer. We had completed the basic engineering order for this customer in the last quarter.

items.statement: First combined contract for ultrapure water and ZLD solutions for a semiconductor company in India; batteries, semiconductors, solar panels (BSS) segment opening opportunities
items.quote: We have received our first combined contract for supply of ultrapure water and ZLD solutions for a semiconductor company in India. This helps in expanding our solutions offerings to new emerging industry segments.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 margins subdued due to volume and mix; 3% material cost improvement offset by 4% increase in other expenses vs Q4 FY26; vs Q1 FY26 material cost up ~10%, other expenses down 7% due to export mix shift to lower-margin African market
items.quote: This quarter, we have seen 3% margin improvement only on the material cost. But at the same time, if you look at my other expenses have gone up by 4%. items.statement: Material cost pressure from geopolitical scenario; using contractual arrangements and advanced procurement to counter; aware of steel cost movement
items.quote: Yes, naturally, there is some kind of an upward trend in the material cost. We are figuring it out, the ways and means of countering that based on either contractual arrangement or having some kind of advanced procurement, which we had done in the earlier years also.

items.statement: Slow backlog conversion due to funding issues and supply-demand imbalance in domestic ethanol is impacting collections; working to improve both execution and collections
items.quote: On collections, the second question that you are asking, because of the slow conversion of some of this backlog, it also has a rubbing effect on the collection of our dues, et cetera. items.statement: Bio-IBA 2% diesel blending mandate potential creates over INR 3,000 crore project opportunity; received order for India's first commercial-scale demo plant
items.quote: Just a 2% blending mandate for Bio-IBA in diesel has a potential to create over INR 3,000 crore project opportunity.

items.statement: Brazil greenfield corn-to-ethanol plant order for ~800 KLPD capacity, end-to-end execution
items.quote: If you're asking about the Brazil part- Sagar: Yes Ashish Gaikwad: then this is almost 800 KLPD type of a capacity. It is a fairly large capacity. It is a corn to ethanol project that we are doing end-to-end

items.statement: Shareholders approved final dividend of 180% per share at AGM
items.quote: In yesterday's AGM, shareholders have approved the payment of final dividend of 180% per share.

items.statement: Funding-related issues persist causing extended project execution cycles; supply-demand imbalance impacting backlog conversion to revenue
items.quote: On the project backlog execution front, Funding-related issues persist, and they are resulting in extended project execution cycles. The supply-demand imbalance has also impacted the project's backlog conversions to revenues.

items.statement: Lifecycle services business growing steadily quarter-over-quarter; conducting performance enhancer trials in Latin America to expand offerings
items.quote: Our lifecycle services business is growing steadily quarter-over-quarter. Via our lifecycle services business, we continue to serve our large customer installed base. We provide physical and digital services that ensure optimal plant performance and

items.quote: We continue to pursue those JVs. We continue to talk about the JV. With the GOBARdhan coming into play, probably, we will be able to speed up some of these discu ssions. Right now, because they are in the play, I would not be speaking too much about it, as far as JVs are concerned

items.statement: CBG feedstock success on press mud, rice straw, Napier grass; viability achieved but continuous quality feedstock supply critical; MSW feedstock challenges remain, not pursuing aggressively

items.quote: Market is still maturing. It is in a very nascent stage. I suppose it is too early to say what is the market share per se. The question which you are asking from the offering point of view, technically, we can offer end-to-end solution in CBG.

items.statement: Cash in hand as of June 30, 2026 was INR 6.16 billion
items.quote: Cash in hand as on June 30, 2026, is INR 6.16 billion.

items.statement: Target ~80% secured AUM by March 2027 including guarantee programs
items.quote: We remain firmly on track towards our objective of approximately 80% secured AUM by March 2027, including loans supported by appropriate guarantee programs.

items.statement: Target 25-30% of monthly business from partnerships
items.quote: We had earlier indicated our objective of generating approximately 25% to 30% of monthly business through direct partnerships, and this channel is now gaining traction.

items.statement: Target renewable energy loans at ~10% of AUM by end of FY27
items.quote: We remain on track with our objective of taking energy loans to approximately 10% of our AUM by the end of FY27.

items.statement: Expect normalized disbursements by Q4 FY27 (January)
items.quote: I think by January, the fourth quarter of this year should see very normalized disbursements.

items.statement: AUM at INR832 crores as of June 2026, 5% YoY underlying growth excluding ARC impact
items.quote: Our AUM stood at INR832 crores as of June 2026. On an underlying basis, AUM grew 5% year-on-year, excluding the ARC impact.

items.statement: Disbursements INR77 crores in Q1 FY27 vs INR92 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Disbursements during the quarter stood at INR77 crores, compared with INR92 crores in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Secured loans 87% of Q1 disbursements vs 67% in FY26
items.quote: Secured loans accounted for 87% of our disbursements during first quarter compared with 67% in FY26.

items.statement: ~70% of disbursements in ticket sizes above INR5 lakhs, ~75% to customers with bureau score 650+
items.quote: Around 70% of disbursement was in ticket sizes above INR5 lakhs, while approximately 75% were to customers with bureau score of 650 and above.

items.statement: Secured book ~75% of AUM including DLG programs vs 49% in June 2025
items.quote: Our secured book now represents approximately 75% of the AUM, including loans backed by default loss guarantee programs compared with 49% in June 2025.

items.statement: Renewable energy cumulative disbursements crossed INR10 crores till July 2026; 15% of July disbursements
items.quote: We crossed INR10 crores of cumulative renewable energy loan disbursements till July '26, reflecting encouraging initial traction. In fact, in July, 15% of the disbursements are through renewable energy loans.

items.statement: Partnership channel at 15% of disbursements last month, targeting 20% by Sep-Oct, 30% by January
items.quote: So, Jhanvi, last month, 15% of the disbursements came through partnership. And I believe in coming months, say, in September and October, this could reach 20% of the monthly business. And by January, 30% at least monthly business should be from the partnership level.

items.statement: NIM 12.3% vs 14.36% in Q1 FY26; interest spread 12%; avg borrowing cost 12.5%
items.quote: Our net interest margin stood at 12.3% compared to 14.36% in quarter 1 of FY26, while our interest spread stood at 12%. The movement in lending yields is consistent with the deliberate shift towards secured products, while our average borrowing cost remained at 12.5%.

items.statement: Solar partnership yield 23%, dairy partnership target ~22% yield
items.quote: So like in Solar, we are getting a yield of 23%. Again, for dairy partnerships, we will be at a yield level, we will try to make about 22%, which is not less than our LAP portfolio.

items.statement: Partnership opex expected 1-1.5% range with FLDG and incentives
items.quote: But on these things, the opex, my understanding is that opex will be in the range of 1% -1.5%. And because there is FLDG and FLDG guarantee program, and sometimes even incentive programs.

items.statement: Moneyboxx One LOS launched May 2026 now live; Sikka, Cattle AI, MBCollect platforms strengthening lending cycle
items.quote: Our proprietary Moneyboxx One loan origination system, which was launched in May 2026 is now live. Sikka mobile application, Cattle AI and MBCollect platforms continue to strengthen different parts of lending cycle.

items.statement: Branch rationalization saving ~INR1-1.25 lakhs per month per closed branch
items.quote: approximately INR1 lakh to INR1.25 lakhs per month which is what you save there. Raj Doshi: Okay. Deepak Aggarwal: Which is the fixed expense on the sale-side and the

items.statement: Plan institutional equity infusion in H2 FY27
items.quote: Additionally, we will look forward to institutional equity infusion in H2 of FY27.

items.statement: Expect <0.5% credit loss in solar segment this year due to OEM/EPC support and secured nature
items.quote: Really, you asked me, we don't see, I mean, more than, say, 0.5% of credit loss in this segment for this year.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 28.65% as of June 2026
items.quote: Our capital adequacy stood at 28.65% as of June 2026, providing us with sufficient headroom to support the growth plan for FY27.

items.statement: Stopped unsecured loans from April 2026 except partnerships and Punjab; stopped secured loans below INR5 lakhs except few solar branches
items.quote: From April 2026 onwards, we stopped disbursement of unsecured loans, except through partnership model and in the state of Punjab. We also stopped disbursement of secured loans below INR5 lakhs, except in few branches of Solar Loans.

items.statement: Unsecured lending down to 13% from 100% at inception due to post-July 2024 MFI guidelines
items.quote: You would notice that unsecured lending has now from 100% of our lending when we started has now come down to 13% because of the changes we saw post July 2024 with guidelines on MFI.

items.statement: Partnerships with Rabo Foundation, Gates Foundation, Water.org, Shell Foundation providing credit protection and incentives
items.quote: Our technological capabilities, together with our para-veterinary services also helped us build partnerships with global institutions like Rabo Foundation, Gates Foundation, Water.org, Shell Foundation and a few others.

items.statement: Dairy partnership with firm that raised INR700 crores PE; digital lending partnership with reputed name
items.quote: The dairy partnership which we are doing is -- has raised INR700 crores private equity from very good firms. It's a reputed name. The digital lending is again a very reputed name.

items.statement: Monitoring geopolitical developments impact via oil prices, shipping costs, customer confidence; taking calibrated growth approach
items.quote: At the same time, we continue to monitor external developments, particularly geopolitical developments and their potential impact through oil prices, shipping costs and customer confidence. While we remain constructive on the underlying opportunity, we are taking a calibrated approach to growth in current environment.

items.statement: Employee count not increasing, decreasing to some extent; teams being trained for higher ticket secured lending
items.quote: Number of employees are not increasing. In fact, to some extent, they are decreasing. So how we are doing it, that we are bringing these kind of partnerships.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 15% despite Q1 growth of ~5%
items.quote: Overall for the year, we still maintain our 15% guidance. We are quite confident we will achieve that.

items.statement: FY27 finance cost expected at 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue after fundraise
items.quote: I believe that this year, our finance cost should be somewhere between 3.2% to 3.5% for the whole year after this fundraise.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance of INR7,000 crores plus, targeting closing order book of INR10,000 crores plus
items.quote: FY27, Navin, I think we should do anything -- we should be able to do INR7,000 crores plus for this year. INR1,600 crores we've already got. So we are well on track. But I think for the full year, INR7,000 crores should be very much possible. And that should take us to a closing order book of INR10,000 crores plus.

items.statement: Polymer segment targeting 20% revenue growth with margin improvement for FY27
items.quote: And we are quite confident that for the full year, we will be able to deliver a 20% improvement -- a 20% growth in top line with some improvement in margins as well.

items.statement: Export order inflow expected to jump more than 50% YoY in FY27, targeting INR1,100 crores
items.quote: We ourselves are expecting more than a 50% jump in export order inflow compared to last year. So this is on the export side, it is definitely much, much more positive compared to last year.

items.statement: Highest ever unexecuted order book of over INR9,200 crores as of Q1 FY27
items.quote: We closed the quarter with our highest ever unexecuted order book of over INR9,200 crores, representing healthy growth over March '26 and providing strong multiyear revenue visibility.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 fresh order inflows of approximately INR1,674 crores; bidding pipeline at all-time high of INR35,000 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured fresh order inflows of approximately INR1,674 crores, while our bidding pipeline expanded to an all -time high level of INR35,000 crores, supported by robust domestic transmission investment and improving opportunities across international markets.

items.statement: Approximately INR5,000 crores of current INR9,200 crores order book expected to be executed in FY27
items.quote: So we believe that in this year, in FY27, out of this INR9,200 crores, approximately INR5,000 crores will be executed.

items.statement: 75,000 ton capacity expansion expected operational by end of Q2 FY27, taking total capacity to 450,000 tons per annum
items.quote: Further, the ongoing 75,000 ton capacity expansion is expected to become operational during the second half of the year, taking our total manufacturing capacity to 450,000 tons per annum, further strengthening our position as the largest power T&D structur e manufacturer in the country

items.statement: Capacity expansion delayed by only a few months, commissioning by end of Q2 FY27, no impact on 15% revenue growth target
items.quote: No. Actually, there's only a few months deferment in the capacity expansion. So we are going to be commissioning by the end of quarter 2. So honestly, we don't see any impact on our overall target of 15% revenue growth this year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 60 bps YoY to 10.7%; long-term aspirational margin of 12%
items.quote: EBITDA increased 10% to INR140 crores with margins expanding by 60 basis points to 10.7%.

items.statement: Margin improvement structural due to legacy low-margin contracts nearly exhausted, better project mix, operational leverage, and commodity hedging
items.quote: So I would say due to all these efforts only, we have dealt with these commodity price fluctuations that are taking place in the market and yet delivering a margin expansion. So that definitely will be structural, and we will consistently move towards our long-term aspirational margin of 12%.

items.statement: Steel prices spiked temporarily but normalized to pre-February levels by May; aluminum prices also moderated; firm and variable price contracts with hedging mitigate commodity impact
items.quote: But by the month of May, we saw the steel prices had normalized to the pre-February or January levels quite a bit. So now they are completely back to the pre -February level. So in steel, there was only a temporary spike. Even aluminum prices have rationed to a quite extent.

items.statement: Domestic transmission bidding expected at INR90,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores in FY27 vs INR50,000-60,000 crores in FY26; intrastate projects now also coming via TBCB route
items.value: INR90,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores
items.quote: We have seen -- we are expecting bids of close to INR90,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores of bids in the Indian transmission market in this financial year.

items.statement: Export demand robust driven by renewables and AI data centers; advanced contract discussions with buyers in developed markets; orders expected from Q2
items.quote: All over the world, there is a very strong push for transmission grid investments, thanks to renewables and AI data centers. In fact, in many locations in the U.S., data centers are not getting clearance because the grid does not have enough power to supply to the new data centers.

items.statement: North America and Australia main export markets for FY27; Europe delayed due to approvals; traditional markets (Middle East, Africa, Latin America) also contributing
items.quote: North America and Australia are going to be our main market. Europe is still going to take some time because we are yet to get our approvals, et cetera, in place. So we are a bit ahead in these two markets, North America and Australia.

items.statement: Export mix target of 50% of order inflow long-term; FY27 export inflow ~15% of total, targeting 20-25% next year
items.quote: And long-term aspirational, just like our margin aspiration is 12%, our export order inflow is also targeted at 50% of our overall order inflow. And we'll get there.

items.statement: INR433.5 crores preferential equity raise completed from global and domestic long-only investors; CRISIL upgraded long-term rating to A+ stable in July
items.quote: We successfully completed a INR433.5 crores preferential equity raise from marquee global and domestic long -only institutional investors, substantially enhancing our financial flexibility. This was followed by CRISIL upgrading our long -term credit rating to A+ stable in July, validating our stronger financial profile, prudent capital allocation and consistent operating performance.

items.statement: Entire QIP proceeds used for debt repayment; finance cost expected to reduce to 3.2-3.5% of revenue in FY27
items.quote: Yes. As of now, see, the entire proceeds, we have used for debt repayment only. And the idea is to strengthen the balance sheet and obviously provide enough ammunition to the company for future capex.

items.statement: Q1 finance cost reduction due to better working capital management and operational leverage, not fundraise (funds received end of July/early August)
items.quote: Our fundraise actually came in the month of -- end of July or in fact, the first week of August is when we received the fund. So quarter 1 did not see any benefit from the fundraise. Whatever improvement you are seeing in the finance cost is purely due to better operational -- better working capital management and overall operational leverage of the company.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be H2 weighted as export logistics normalize, capacity utilization improves, and recent orders move into execution
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect FY27 to be H2 weighted. As export logistics normalized, capacity utilization improved and recently secured orders move into execution, we expect stronger growth momentum during the second half.

items.statement: New 75,000 ton capacity primarily export-focused; export order intake was poor last year but expecting 50% jump this year
items.quote: See, bulk of our new capacity that we have built up last year also the 75,000 tons capacity, which we built up is primarily focused on exports. And export order intake was poor last year.

items.statement: Secured two 765 kV projects from reputed developer in Maharashtra; completed qualification audits for developed market customers including USA, Finland, Australia; established subsidiaries in Brazil and UAE
items.quote: We secured two 765 kV projects from a reputed developer in the state of Maharashtra and successfully completed qualification audits and from developed market customers, including U.S.A., Finland and Australia, while strengthening our international presence with establishment of subsidiaries in Brazil and UAE.

items.statement: New players and foreign capital entering TBCB market (I Squared's CubeGrid, NIIF's AnantGrid); bidding activity robust with many bids already floated
items.quote: And in fact, in the sector, the large number of new players, new developers are also coming in. A lot of foreign capital has also been coming in by -- if you have heard -- you might have heard of I Squared, which has set up a platform, CubeGrid, then NIIF, which is the sovereign government of India fund, they have launched a new fund -- they have launched a new platform called AnantGrid.

items.statement: Biggest challenge is quality manpower recruitment and retention in technical roles; hiring 200-250 graduate trainees annually with robust training program
items.quote: I would say the biggest challenge is quality manpower, especially in the technical side, both on the manufacturing as well as the project side. And definitely because there is so much of spurt in demand that has taken place. So recruiting and retaining quality manpower is probably the biggest challenge and which keeps us awake at night.

items.statement: Short-term export orders challenged by high shipping costs causing shipment deferrals; domestic and export short-term orders may spike later in year as players face capacity constraints
items.quote: However, short-term orders right now are a challenge in terms of export market at least because, like I said, export customers, even the ones where we have orders ri ght now, they are deferring shipments because they don't want to bear the increased shipping

items.statement: Only ~40% of INR9 lakh crores total transmission bids (FY22-32) have been bid so far; annual bidding run-rate of INR90,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores expected
items.quote: So our estimate is so far about -- just about 40% of the total bids of INR9 lakh crores have been bidded so far.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of 500 crores, implying 33% growth
items.quote: For the complete FY27, we expect 33% revenue growth, reaching the 500-crore mark.

items.statement: FY27 PBDIT margin expected to improve by 300 basis points over previous year
items.quote: While PBDIT moderated in Q1, we expect the full-year PBDIT margin to improve by around 300 basis points over the previous year.

items.statement: Targeting land acquisition for 100,000-ton capacity by end of FY27
items.quote: We are targeting to acquire that piece of land by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Next greenfield project initiation targeted for Q3 FY28, fundraising in Q1/Q2 FY28
items.quote: We might initiate the next project by Q3 of next year. Fundraising in Q1 or Q2 of 2028 would be the ideal time.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capacity utilization at 66% on expanded 45,000-ton capacity; targeting 80% for full year
items.quote: Since expanding the capacity to 45,000 tons per annum, we have already reached 66% capacity utilization in the first quarter. We are ramping up and expect to reach 80% utilization of the complete new capacity for the entire year of FY27.

items.statement: July utilization reached 85% (3,200 tons); expect 80-90% within 2-3 months
items.quote: In July, our utilization reached 85%, touching 3,200 tons of production. We expect to reach 80-90% utilization within 2-3 months.

items.statement: Machining facility at 50% product development completion and 50% capacity utilization
items.quote: On the machining side, we have completed 50% of product development and hit 50% capacity utilization last month.

items.statement: MSEDCL revised solar banking policy from April, causing 30-40% solar generation loss and retrospective charges; 5MW wind PPA signed via open access to offset
items.quote: in April, MSEDCL revised their policy regarding the banking of solar systems. Previously, power generated between 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM could be used anytime. From April, they stopped allowing the banking of these units to other zones. We lost around 30- 40% of the energy generated by our solar as lapsed units. Additionally, MSEDCL implemented this policy with a retrospective measure following a cour

items.statement: Executable order book positioned at 500 crores for FY27; 600 crores executable next year with same products and customers
items.quote: We now refer to it as an executable order book. For the current year, we have positioned it at 500 crores considering various hurdles. If we move into the next financial year with higher capacity, we should be able to execute 600 crores with the same products and customers.

items.statement: Nordex NX N series 5MW platform prototypes cleared in Q1; purchase orders for US market exports coming in good numbers
items.quote: We received clearance for the Nordex NX N series 5-megawatt platform prototypes in the first quarter. We already have purchase orders mainly for US market exports, and it is coming in very good numbers.

items.statement: Vestas 4MW platform tooling development started mid-May; samples expected Q4 FY27, full production Q1 FY28
items.quote: we are working on the 4-megawatt platform. We signed this contract in mid-May and have started tooling development. The earlier 3-megawatt platform is being phased out. We expect samples to move in Q4 of this financial year, with full-fledged production in Q1 of next year

items.statement: Received orders for coal-based power plants from L&T and BHEL; BHEL PO received this quarter, development 8-9 months
items.quote: We received orders for coal-based power plants from L&T and BHEL. L&T development is underway, and we received the BHEL PO this quarter. BHEL is a critical import substitute and may take 8-9 months to develop.

items.statement: Strong mining order book from Terex due to 20% Yen appreciation vs Rupee making Indian suppliers 5-10% cheaper on landed cost
items.quote: mining sector, we are seeing a strong order book from Terex due to currency depreciation. The 20% Yen appreciation against the Rupee has tilted the game in favor of Indian suppliers over China. We believe we are 5% to 10% cheaper on a landed cost basis for wind products

items.statement: Vestas accounts for 40-45% of business, may reduce to 30% as new OEMs added; Nordex becoming sizable contributor
items.quote: Vestas has been our largest for 15 years, sometimes accounting for over 40-45% of business. As we add more clients and capacity, their share might come down to 30%, though the absolute revenue will not drop. Nordex is becoming a sizable contributor.

items.statement: New OEMs like Nordex and Adani can each allocate 100-150 crores; non-wind and gearboxes contribute ~30% of revenue
items.quote: Vestas is asking for more allocation, but we are committing capacity to new OEMs like Nordex and Adani. These new OEMs can each allocate 100 to 150 crores. Non-wind and gearboxes contribute closer to 30% of revenue, leaving about 400 crores for wind.

items.statement: US market projects incentivized for non-Chinese suppliers; customers pressuring not to divert capacity
items.quote: We have big commitments in the wind sector, particularly for the US market, where projects are incentivized for non-Chinese suppliers. These customers are putting pressure on us not to divert capacity.

items.statement: Realizations expected to reflect inflation in upcoming quarters, moving from 138-140 to 145-plus levels
items.quote: Realizations should reflect the inflation in upcoming quarters, moving from 138-140 to 145-plus levels.

items.statement: Inventory increased due to shipping constraints and prototype approvals; production not converted to sales yet
items.quote: Everything produced was not sold, leading to an increase in inventory due to shipping constraints and prototype approvals. We have produced the material; it is only a matter of revenue recognition.

items.statement: Target keeping order book below 8 weeks' inventory in shop; generally carry 8-10 weeks inventory
items.quote: Generally, we carry an inventory of 8 to 10 weeks. We target keeping the order book below 8 weeks' inventory in our shop.

items.statement: ISTS waiver delay to June 30, 2028 immaterial; policy shifts favor wind with 50% tariff differentiation (25% higher night tariffs, 25% solar daytime discount)
items.quote: The wind industry currently has much higher demand than solar. The waiver delay to June 30th, 2028, is immaterial because policy shifts now favor wind. Wind generates electricity at night, and tariffs are now 25% higher at night while solar daytime tariffs are at a 25% discount. This 50% tariff differentiation is a strong incentive for wind installations.

items.statement: India wind annual installation reached record 6.34 GW in FY26; 2030 target 77 GW from current 51 GW
items.quote: India's wind annual installation growth reached a record high of 6.34 gigawatts in FY26. The installed wind capacity in 2030 is expected to reach 77 gigawatts from the current 51 gigawatts.

items.statement: Global wind annual installation grew 40% in 2025 to 165 GW; 2030 cumulative capacity projected >2 TW at 5.2% CAGR
items.quote: Global wind annual installation growth was 40% in 2025, with 165 gigawatts installed globally. By 2030, the global cumulative capacity is projected to exceed 2 terawatts, driven by Synergy Green Industries Limited August 13, 2026 2 a 5.2% CAGR over the next five years

items.statement: Kharagpur plant at 30-35% utilisation with 150-acre free land; Kamarhati plant constrained and loaded
items.quote: Kharagpur plant is loaded only 30%, 35%. It's not loaded beyond that. So there's a very significant jump possible in that with some bridging capex.

items.statement: Large debt on balance sheet; working capital cycle easing expected to reduce debt; no specific repayment numbers given
items.quote: we are also carrying a large debt on our balance sheet and our profitability is not as high as of now to sustain all to service th is sort of debt. So when can we see our working capital cycle easing out and thereby reduction in our debt

items.statement: Tulip serves ~80% of city gas distribution network; one-third market share in CNG stations; key clients include IGL, Mahanagar Gas, Indraprastha Gas; defense serves Army, Navy, Air Force, DRDO, VRDE
items.quote: Tulip's offerings are going today to almost 80% of the country everywhere. Wherever city gas distribution is there, wherever you see a gas station dispensing CNG, chances are in one-third of those stations we are already there.

items.statement: Chinese competitors have pricing and credit advantages; TIL differentiates on reliability, durability, aftermarket uptime commitment; avoids extended credit terms
items.quote: strategy is very clear. One, we will bring in products which are required by the customer, but not on offer. We will bring in products which are more reliable. We will bring in products which are more durable

items.statement: Monsoon outlook positive till September; next 20 days critical for kharif crop survival and rabi moisture
items.quote: So the outlook is good. But the next 15 to 20 days is going to be critical because the standing crops have to survive.

items.statement: FY27 outlook too early; will comment in a month
items.quote: I think it's a little too early. I would say, I will be able to comment on that in another month's time.

items.statement: Tiller volume growth 16-20% to continue at least till September; power weeder 50-60% growth to continue
items.quote: We are talking anywhere between 16% to 20% for the last few quarters now. That will continue. The power weeder segment, we have been clocking 50% to 60% growth for the last several quarters now. That will continue.

items.statement: Q1 tractor production ramp-up limited supply; Q2-Q4 substantial volume increase expected
items.quote: In Q1, we have not been able to fully supply to the demand that was there. So the numbers look small. So that, I would say, would have been better if the production would have been ramped up. So Q2, you will find that growing again and Q3, Q4, substantial volume increase we are expecting.

items.statement: Target upwards of 15,000 tractors, close to 20,000 by FY30 including 5,000-6,000 international
items.quote: I have in last call also, in the last quarter I have said upwards of 15,000 numbers we will aim to reach, close to 20,000 numbers we will aim to reach in FY '30.

items.statement: Launching 30+ tractor variants in next 3 years; FENTM series expanding to Maharashtra; VZ production ramping
items.quote: In the next 3 years, we are talking about launching more than 30 variants of tractors, various products that we will be launching in the next 3 years.

items.statement: New production facility investment in next 2 years to support INR3,000 cr revenue vision by 2030
items.quote: We will have to also invest in new production facility in the next 2 years or so.

items.statement: Revenue vision INR3,000 crores by 2030
items.quote: INR3,000 crores is our vision. We will be achieving that by 2030.

items.statement: Tractor dealership expansion: added 40-50 last year, targeting 50-60 this year focused on North India
items.quote: Last year we added 40, 50 dealers across India. This year we are targeting about 50 to 60 dealers across India.

items.statement: SFM counter expansion: added 500+ counters in 3 months; target 2,000 counters by year-end
items.quote: By the end of this year, we would like to expand the retail counters to about 2,000 counters.

items.statement: US expansion unclear due to potential 100% tariff; electric tractor plans on back seat
items.quote: The reality is it's very difficult to predict 3 weeks now. So to be realistic, because if something like 100% tariff comes up on the new bill that is going through the U.S. Congress. Now that could be a big trouble in our expansion plans into the U.S. market.

items.statement: New tiller-tractor hybrid product rolling out this month; substantial volumes in Q3-Q4; price close to tiller, work close to tractor
items.quote: The first of those products will roll out of the factory from this month onwards. And we should be able to do substantial volume in Q3 and Q4 on those products.

items.statement: Geared tiller with differential for European market; EV tillers and weeders for international markets
items.quote: It will be a tiller which can give us good growth in the international market. That is number one. Number two, we are also looking at EV, that is electric tillers and weeders which we believe will have a market internationally as well.

items.statement: Retail financing via Bajaj Finance doubled to ~1,000 units (8-9% of retail); target 15-20% this year; partnerships with Chola, TVS, Bajaj, nationalized banks
items.quote: This year the volume has gone up in terms of retail financing. We have sold close to 1,000 through retail financing compared to just about 400-odd numbers we did Q1 of last year. So it has almost doubled. However, our business has also grown. So the percentage is at around 8% to 9% of retail. We wanted to grow it to about 15% to 20% this year.

items.statement: TREM Stage 5 (<25HP) from Oct'26 ready; TREM 3AA from Apr'28 ready; full Stage 5 by 2032 ready; cost impact 25-30% at current tech
items.quote: Stage 5 for all products less than 25 horsepower, both for tillers as well as tractors. And VST is fully prepared for it and completely ready for it. Then the next implementation in TREM 3AA from April '28, which also VST will be fully prepared.

items.statement: Stage 5 emission tech currently costs 25-30% of tractor cost; expected to decline over time with global volumes
items.quote: The current cost of that technology on the tractor is about 25%, 30% of -- it will go up. But that is the current cost. How technology will evolve, how costly or cheaper will that be in 2032 is difficult for me to say at this point in time.

items.statement: Q1 operational EBITDA 12.85% (INR40.3 cr) vs 13.3% last year; 45 bps drop due to raw material inflation
items.quote: Operational EBITDA where we exclude the other income and fair value gain from the EBITDA is standing at 12.85%. In terms of rupees crores, it is INR40.3 crores. Last year same period, it was 13.3%. So there is a drop of around 45 basis points.

items.statement: Commodity cost inflation in steel, forging, casting, aluminum, copper; natural rubber elevated and volatile; crude and freight high
items.quote: We also have commodity cost inflation -related trends for all steel, forging, casting, aluminum, copper. Natural rubber also -- prices of natural rubber also remain elevated and volatile. Due to the geopolitical and supply chain -related disruption, crude and freight costs remain high.

items.statement: Capital allocation policy to maximize shareholder value; exploring deployment opportunities in next 18-24 months; no development on non-core asset sale
items.quote: The policy is very clear to maximize shareholder value. That's very clear. That means that the deployment of the capital that we have should be done strategically and we are exploring several opportunities for deploying that capital. Hopefully, in the next 18 to 24 months, we should have some good deployment of this capital.

items.statement: Inorganic opportunities too early to comment; will update as things progress
items.quote: It's too early to say anything at this point, and we will keep you posted as things progress.

items.statement: Power tiller volume grew ~18%; domestic tractor volume grew 4.5%; tractor exports 275 units; power weeder grew 56%
items.quote: I'm happy to mention that during the quarter, the power tiller business has grown to roughly 18% of growth in terms of volume. Also, our domestic tractor business has grown b y 4.5%. However, in case of tractor export, in the current quarter, we have sold 275 tractors. Power weeder has recorded an impressive growth of 56

items.statement: Management targets 20-25% top-line and PAT growth for FY27, with potential for ~50% as customer confidence grows
items.quote: As a promoter, I would want it to be a lot. I can see 20% to 25% growth, but as customer confidence grows, it could be around 50%. But a 20% to 25% increase in top line and PAT is also increasing and will continue to increase.

items.statement: Current year target is to reach 10,000 orders per day and expand quick delivery to additional cities
items.quote: Our ambitious for Womancart extends well behind our current scale. We want to build Womancart into a commerce and lifestyle commerce platform for the woman with the comprehensive offering fashion, beauty, wellness, home and everything on their lifestyle. Dear friends, just going to complete my current year target is to reach 10,000 orders per day and progressively expand our quick delivery proposi

items.statement: PAT margin improved to 11.5% in Q1 FY27 reflecting better earnings conversion and operating leverage
